DOC1 INTRODUCTION

General Information

The information contained in this document applies only to the software versions indicated on the title page.
Not all functions provided by the product may be described in this documentation; in such cases, Donatoni Macchine is not obliged to guarantee these functions or preserve them in future versions.
This document is provided as attachment “Section B”, software section, of the machine use and maintenance manual.

Purpose of the manual

This manual contains the operating instructions required for a proper understanding of the Parametrix program and useful information for troubleshooting malfunctions.
Proper operation, service life and operating economy of the machine depend on compliance with the instructions described in this manual.
The machine use and maintenance manual and this software manual must always be available at the installation site, kept in a safe and easily accessible place. If either is lost, contact the person responsible for the prevention and protection service.
Failure to comply with the instructions described in this manual, negligence, or improper and inadequate use of the machine may result in cancellation, by the Manufacturer, of the warranty provided for the machine and may also prevent the machine from delivering the benefits for which it was designed.
DONATONI MACCHINE SRL is available to provide prompt and accurate technical assistance and any support that may be useful for ensuring optimum machine operation and maximum performance.
The Manufacturer reserves the right, at its own discretion, to modify this publication and the data contained herein whenever it deems this necessary for technical or commercial improvement of the product.

Manual storage

This Software Manual must be kept throughout the entire operating life of the machine, including in the event of transfer to third parties.
To ensure proper storage of the Software Manual, the following is recommended:

  • Use the Manual in such a way as not to damage all or part of its contents; in particular, do not leave the Manual unattended during use and return it to its designated place immediately after consultation;

  • Do not remove, tear out or rewrite any part of the Manual for any reason;

  • Keep the Manual in areas protected from moisture, heat and other environmental agents that could compromise its integrity or service life;

  • If all or part of this Manual is lost or damaged, request a copy of the documentation from the Manufacturer.

DOC2 ON-MACHINE PROGRAMS

When the application starts, if the axes have already been zeroed, the following initial screen is displayed:

Top bar

Parameters
Provides access to the Parametrix program parameters.

Parameters tool
Pressing the button opens the tool parameters page. See the “Tool Configuration” chapter for a detailed description of the parameters page.

Automatic 0/90-degree rotation
The “C” axis is automatically moved to either 0 or 90 degrees when the button is pressed.

Automatic parking
When pressed, the machine automatically moves the “X”, “Y”, “Z” and “C” axes to their zero positions.
The machine performs the movements in the following order:
(A) - “Z” axis to the absolute zero position;
(B) - “C” axis to the absolute 0 position;
(C) - “X” and “Y” axes simultaneously to the absolute zero position;

WARNING!

Certain safety conditions must be met in order to perform automatic parking:
The “A” axis position must be 0_.
Make sure that the movement area involved in positioning (see figure alongside) is clear.

Internal water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply through the inside of the tool.
The indicator above the button changes color: Green = On; Red = Off.

External water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply from the main line.
The indicator above the button changes color: Green = On; Red = Off.

Manual Tool Change
Pressing the button starts the tool change procedure.

Maintenance
Pressing this button displays a window containing all machine maintenance operations.
Both maintenance operations that need to be performed and those within normal limits are displayed.

Help
Pressing this button slightly changes the appearance and behavior of all buttons currently visible. You can then press any button with a small question mark in the upper-left corner to learn about the function provided by that button through a short message. To exit this help mode, simply press the “Help” button again.

Common interface elements

The graphical interface elements common to the functions are:

Axes

This interface displays the machine axis values.

Example of the “Axes” interface element with origin 0 and the axes already zeroed:

Example of the “Axes” interface element with origin 0 and the axes not yet zeroed:

The elements making up this section of the common interface are explained below, using the elements shown when the axes have already been zeroed as reference.

Actual position: indicates the axis position relative to the active origin.
Target position: indicates the position to be set in order to move the axis by pressing the MDI or RTCP button.
F: Feed, movement speed expressed in mm/minute.
DTG: Distance To Go, distance from the target.
A: Ampere.

Axis Reset
Pressing this button sets the zero point of the active origin at the current position of the corresponding axis (X, Y or Z).
The axis reset operation can only be performed on origins other than 0 (zero).
To use the tool-coordinate origin (TCP), the correct dimensions of the mounted tool must be set before pressing the Axis Reset button.

Automatic _90-degree rotation
The “C” axis position is increased by 90 degrees clockwise.
Example: if the machine is at 12 degrees, pressing the “Automatic _90-degree rotation” button moves the machine to 102 degrees: 12 _ 90.

Automatic -90-degree rotation
The “C” axis position is decreased by 90 degrees counterclockwise.
Example: if the machine is at 102 degrees, pressing the “Automatic -90-degree rotation” button moves the machine to 12 degrees: 102 - 90.

Controls

This panel contains several buttons whose behavior is explained below:

Interpolation mode
When the button is active (figure on the right), manual Z, C and A movements are performed taking rotation and inclination into account.
Interpolated Z-axis movement: when the Z-axis JOG is operated, the machine moves aligned with the mounted tool.

NOTE

The selected tool type affects the direction of movement.

Interpolated C-axis movement: when the C-axis control is operated, in addition to rotation the X and Y axes also move so that the inner edge of the blade (or the tool tip) remains stationary.
Interpolated A-axis movement: when the A-axis control is operated, in addition to inclination the X, Y and Z axes also move so that the inner edge of the blade (or the tool tip) remains stationary at its current position.
Simultaneous movement of the Z, C and A axes is not permitted when interpolated mode is active.

WARNING!

Pay close attention to the state of the button, as machine movements may differ from what is expected.

RTCP interpolation
Performs positioning to the “Target” position set for the A or C axis while keeping the inner edge of the blade (or the tool tip) stationary.
For further details, see the paragraph: “RTCP Semi-Automatic Function - Rotation Tool Center Point”

MDI
When pressed, the machine moves until the positions set as target positions are reached (see above).
The speed of the X and Y axes is controlled by their respective potentiometers, while the other axes are controlled by the interpolated potentiometer.

Tool

This interface element displays the main information about the tool mounted on the machine.

Example of tool mounted on the machine: Disk

Example of tool mounted on the machine: Core drill

Active tool
Clicking this button displays a confirmation pop-up that allows the operator to change the type of tool mounted on the machine.

The choice is limited to:

  1. Disk

  2. Milling cutter / Core drill

Origin

Clicking the “Origin” field displays a small on-screen numeric keypad that allows the operator to select a different origin to work with.
Origin values can range from 0 to 19 inclusive.

Example with origin 0:

Example with origin 10:

Advanced origin settings

Pressing the options button above the origin opens a panel containing a centralized view of all available origins and their associated values. The active origin can be changed by clicking the corresponding row.

RTCP - Rotation Tool Center Point

The RTCP function allows the operator to position the machine for a miter cut while keeping the tool height unchanged, even though the inclination changes during positioning. The inner edge of the disk remains in the same position as at the start of the movement.

Operating procedure

  • Set the target position in the area dedicated to the “A” axis (inclination) or “C” axis.

  • Pressing the RTCP button starts the inclination or rotation function while keeping the lowest point of the tool fixed.

NOTE

Movement using the RTCP command is permitted only when the coded key is inserted in the designated position on the operator console.

  • Wait for the machine to reach the set position.

Motor

This section provides some statistics relating to the machine motor:

Revolutions per minute (RPM)
The value indicates the spindle motor revolutions per minute. If the direction of rotation is clockwise, the value is positive; if the direction is counterclockwise, the sign is negative.

Consumption (A)
Indicates the current drawn by the spindle motor.

Alarm threshold (A)
Indicates the threshold above which the alarm is activated and spindle rotation is stopped.

Feed

The Feed value represents the interpolated movement of the machine.

Right sidebar

When the application starts, the preselected function is MANUAL.
This sidebar contains the following available commands and programs/functions:

Bottom bar

The bottom bar displays information and error messages as well as buttons for certain functions.
Three examples of the bottom bar are shown below:

  • With no active alarms.

  • With a general emergency active, shown with an icon, an error code (PE0000 in this example), the related description, and the alarm button on the right flashing.

  • With a displayed message, direct JOG active in the example.

Alarms
Allows the operator to access the alarm window.

Minimize software
Allows the operator to exit the software page.

Machine shutdown
Allows the operator to completely shut down the machine.

Alarms

The alarms page shows the active system Alarms/Messages.
If the machine has no active alarms, the page is empty; otherwise, one row is displayed for each current error.
The following example page for alarm management and display shows an alarm currently active in the system:

Alarm buttons

Updates
Used to refresh the status of the machine alarms.

Alarm history
Allows the daily alarm history to be displayed.

Messages / Alarms
Allows you to choose whether to display alarms or messages.

Alarm groups
Shows complete information about the alarms currently present on the machine.

Alarm display - Standard

The standard display of one of the alarms consists of:

Online link
A button with a link to the relevant online guide.

Alarm code
Identification code of the problem that caused the alarm.

Description
A brief description of the detected error.

Alarm display - History

In addition to the items already described, the daily alarm history also includes the following data:

Status change time
Date and time when the alarm status changed.

Alarm status
Status reached by the alarm (ON / OFF).

Alarm display - Groups

The grouping system displays a single entry for each alarm, avoiding duplicates.

Number of occurrences
The number of times the alarm has been activated.

First activation time
Date and time of the first alarm activation.

Last activation time
Date and time of the most recent alarm activation.

DOC2.1 MANUAL (SUCTION CUPS)

The suction cups can be used manually to move pieces from one work zone to another.

Suction cup buttons

Enable / disable suction cups
The screen shows the suction cup assembly viewed from above, divided into its various zones. Pressing the relevant area changes its status.
Green indicates that the zone is set for vacuum.
Red indicates that the zone is set for blowing.

SUCTION CUPS: RAISE - Suction cup parking
When the button is pressed, the suction cups are retracted to the rest/parking position.

SUCTION CUPS: LOWER - Prepare suction cups
When the button is pressed, the suction cups are lowered from the parking position to the limit stop. It is important that there is enough space for the suction cups to extend completely.

LIFT PIECE: RELEASE - Unload piece
When the button is pressed, the Z axis is lowered until the material contacts the work surface, the vacuum pump is switched off, and blowing is activated from all suction cups to release the piece. After a timeout, the axis is raised to the safety position.

LIFT PIECE: START - Lift piece
With this command, the suction cups are brought into contact with the material, the vacuum pump is switched on in the areas marked green and blowing is activated in the areas marked red; once the vacuum switch indicates that vacuum has been generated, the axis is raised to the position set for movements.

WARNING!

Pay attention to the active suction cups and use the largest possible area to lift the piece.

BLOW - Blow control
The button switches blowing on or off from suction cups that are not set for vacuum. The indicator shows whether blowing is on (green) or off (red).

VACUUM - Vacuum pump control
This button switches the vacuum pump on and off. The indicator shows whether the pump is on (green) or off (red).

Safety conditions

Pay particular attention to the active suction cups during lifting, ensuring that the areas used are sufficient to lift the piece being moved. Always try to use the largest available vacuum area to grip the piece and check that there are no defects or breaks in the material that could create hazards or machine operating problems.
Once the vacuum pump has been switched on, it may only be switched off using the automatic functions provided for this purpose. Pressing the reset button or the emergency stop mushroom has no effect on the vacuum pump, which will continue to operate. The pump can be forcibly switched off using the dedicated button on the “Additional Controls” page.
During automatic procedures, before lifting the piece, the vacuum status is checked by a dedicated sensor: if a sufficient vacuum value is not detected, the “vacuum missing” alarm appears. The pump will remain active until the vacuum switch detects a correct value or until it is disabled from the “Additional Controls” page.

WARNING!

Loss of power to the vacuum pump causes a rapid loss of vacuum and consequently causes the material lifted by the suction cups to fall.

DOC2.2 SINGLE CUT

In newer versions of Parametrix, the “Single Cut” function can be used. Selecting “Single Cut” from the list opens a page similar to the following.

Single Cut can be used to perform a straight cut (or a miter cut) on the slab, starting from the machine's current position and ending at the length requested by the user. Arcs or circles CANNOT be cut using this function.

Buttons

Parallel cut buttons
Allows parallel movement of the machine.

Max
Pressing this button sets the effective cutting length to the distance between the current machine position and the end of the slab (the end of the slab is calculated based on the machine's current direction).
This value may differ from the value entered by the user in the text box.

Stop
Used after the machine has started cutting when the cutting length needs to be reduced. Pressing this button stops the machine and enters the length of the path cut so far in the “Length” text box.
Alternatively, the dedicated button on the console can be pressed to obtain the same behavior as the STOP button.

Change Step Mode
Switches between “full pass” mode and “step pass” mode and vice versa.

Save
Pressing this button will save all the parameters within a file in order to retrieve them later.

Open
Pressing this button displays a window containing all jobs previously saved by the user.
The jobs can be managed by loading values, deleting jobs, or canceling the operation and closing the panel.

Parameters

Depending on the type of material to be machined, the parameters can be set differently and saved for subsequent similar jobs.

 

Common parameters

Single-cut length
The length of the cut to be performed must be entered before the operation can be carried out. If the value exceeds what can actually be cut, the machine stops earlier.

Movement distance
Indicates the distance between one cut and the next. Only positive values can be entered in this field. For leveling, it is recommended to set a “movement distance” equal to approximately 80% of the tool thickness.

Pass machining configuration parameters

Penetration into the material when moving forward
Indicates the cutting depth in the material when the machine cuts in the direction of disk rotation.

Penetration into the material when moving backward
Indicates the cutting depth in the material during cutting in the direction opposite to the tool direction.

Penetration into the material for the last pass
Indicates the cutting depth required for the last tool pass on the material. This cut is always performed in the direction opposite to disk movement.

Machining speed when moving forward
Indicates the desired speed for the forward cutting phase.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

Machining speed when moving backward
Indicates the desired speed for the return cutting phase.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

Material entry speed
Determines the speed during the tool penetration phase into the material.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

Last-pass machining speed
Indicates the speed the machine must maintain during the cut on the last pass.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

 

Full-pass machining configuration parameters

Material entry speed
Determines the speed during the tool penetration phase into the material.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

Machining speed when moving forward
Indicates the desired speed for the forward cutting phase.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

Executing the machining operation

To start the machining operation, first position the machine at the desired starting point. Once it is positioned correctly, enter the cutting length value in the dedicated field.

At this point, the disk can be switched on using the controls on the monitor control panel. When everything is ready, start the process by pressing the “Cycle Start” button.

The machining operation starts in the direction the machine is facing when the cut is activated, so it is important to check its orientation before starting the cycle.

DOC2.3 ISO PROGRAM

The ISO file programming page is used to manage and start machining operations via .pgm files previously created using CAD-CAM programs.

List

Clear list

Move selected item up
Moves the selected ISO file upward within the list of files to be executed.

Move selected item down

At the bottom there are also two buttons relating to program execution modes:

Manual / automatic

Defines whether the next program will start automatically or not.

Open file

  • Files List

  • Selected Files List

  • Selected File preview

    • Shows a preview of a .pgm file selected from Files or Selected Files

  • Bottom bar and search filter

Central buttons, located between the “FILES” list and the “SELECTED FILES” list

Select item

Remove item

Insert pause

The contents of the bottom bar are shown below:

Sort by last modified

Alphabetical sorting

Show USB drive files

Show ISO folder

Remove file

ISO Program Code

The code of the ISO program currently running is displayed in this window:

Buttons

This section of the ISO program contains the following buttons and related functions.

Timer and Reset
Indicates the execution time of the entire .pgm file.
Pressing the button resets the Timer

View ISO
Enables or disables the ISO preview display.

Block search
This button is displayed only after at least one program has been loaded into the list and allows a block to be searched by line.

Search block by line
This button replaces the “Block search” button after the latter is pressed.
A small on-screen window allows the operator to search for a specific line of code.

After entering a number in the “Line number” field and pressing the “Go to” button, the ISO program code display moves to the requested line, or to the last available line if the entered number exceeds the number of lines in the selected ISO program.

The block search can be ended and the “Block search” button made visible again by pressing the Close button:

Dry Run function (Enabled / disabled)
Selecting this operating mode makes it possible to perform a machining operation at the machine's maximum speed.

WARNING!

Use of this function requires that NO type of material be used during machining because the speeds specified in the ISO program are not observed during execution; the numerical control executes the entire program at the maximum nominal speed achievable with interpolated axes.

ISO Test function (Enabled / disabled)
This option can be used to test the loaded file and check that there are no syntax errors.
Press the “CYCLE START” button and the machine will virtually execute all lines of code without moving the axes.

Suction cup panel
Provides access to the suction cup management panel.

Save
When the button is pressed, a keyboard appears allowing the loaded .pgm file to be edited before it is executed.

Block search

While executing (.pgm) files, the block search function may be useful for repositioning the tool at the point where the machine stopped program execution, for example if the tool becomes stuck in the material or another type of stoppage occurs.

Once the button has been pressed, the line from which to resume/start machining can be searched by line number by pressing the “Search block by line” button, or by scrolling through the file using the scroll bar alongside the file and selecting the desired line.
After selecting the point in the program from which the machine will resume the interrupted work, press the “Cycle Start” button; the machine recalculates all lines of code in the .pgm file without performing any movement. The speed of this operation depends on the number of lines of code that must be generated without performing any movement.

When recalculation is complete, the machine activates an automatic pause, requiring the “Cycle Start” button to be pressed again to start machining.
Before starting the cycle, it is recommended to consider the initial machine positioning, which involves all axes simultaneously.
This is necessary because the machine moves from its current position to the point where machining begins by taking the shortest path, and all axes therefore move to reach that exact point.


This means, for example, that the Z axis does not lower only after reaching the starting point, but lowers gradually along the path. This could damage the machine or the material if the machine collides with material located along the path.
Depending on the current situation, movement of one or more axes can therefore be deselected to prevent damage.
To do this, simply select the buttons above each axis; they change from green to red.

The buttons automatically return to green once “Cycle Start” is pressed.

View ISO

If the ISO preview has been enabled, an additional panel similar to the one shown below is displayed to the right of the “ISO Program Code” panel:

The ISO preview provides the following buttons:

Perspective View
Provides a 3D representation of the image.

View orthogonal to the XY plane
Provides a representation of the piece relative to the XY plane.

View orthogonal to the ZX plane
Provides a representation of the piece relative to the ZX plane.

View orthogonal to the ZY plane
Provides a representation of the piece relative to the ZY plane.

Enable or disable preview display
Enables/disables the preview display.

Executing the machining operation

The operator can create a list of PGM files by opening the desired files using the dedicated load function.

Before starting execution, the order of the files in the list can optionally be changed and pauses can be inserted between executions. These pauses make the process more flexible to manage and, if necessary, allow it to be stopped safely.

When the execution mode is set to "Automatic", the "ISO Test" function is also available and can be used to verify the correctness of the selected ISO program before actual execution.

To start the execution cycle, the operator must press the “Cycle Start” button. This executes the first ISO program loaded and displayed in the list.

ISO programs can be executed in two operating modes:

“Single” mode stops program execution at the end of each ISO file. The “Cycle Start” button must be pressed again to execute the next file in the list.

“Next Automatic” mode executes the ISO files sequentially, without requiring manual intervention, until the end of the list.

In both modes, any pauses inserted between files allow the operator to stop the cycle at any time, thereby maintaining continuous control over execution.

DOC2.4 LEVELING

The leveling cycle can be used to level the workbench or the material. This program is useful when the workbench has become uneven due to cuts, or when the material thickness needs to be made uniform.

Leveling parameters

Movement position relative to the X axis
Positive and negative values can be set.

Movement position relative to the Y axis
Positive and negative values can be set.

Movement distance
Indicates the distance between one cut and the next. Only positive values can be entered in this field. For leveling, it is recommended to set a “movement distance” equal to approximately 80% of the tool thickness.

Depth
Indicates how far to move down during the leveling cycle relative to the acquired position.

Z Step
Indicates the maximum downward step into the material. Depending on the leveling depth, the Z increment may decrease so that all passes are performed at the same depth.

Plunge cutting speed
Indicates the working speed on the Z axis during the automatic cycle; it is expressed in (mm/Min).

Forward cutting speed
Indicates the working speed on the XY plane during the automatic cycle; it is expressed in (mm/Min).

Change tool origin
Pressing this button switches between the disk origin calculated using the line laser and the core-drill origin calculated using the cross laser.

Executing the machining operation

The “LEVELING” program does not require zeroing of the X, Y and Z origins.
The tool position at the time the cycle is started is used to determine the starting position.
After setting the various parameters, move the running disk to the maximum desired depth of the workbench or material and start the cycle using the CYCLE START button.

NOTE

The program can be used with the “A” axis inclination at ZERO degrees or NINETY degrees so that tools such as disks or milling cutters can be used.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC2.5 POCKET

The pocket page is used to machine a rectangular pocket with fillets and a flat bottom.
A suitable milling cutter mounted on the main spindle must be used for this machining operation.
The “workbench level” is used as the bottom level.
The cycle uses pass mode with a helical entry at the center and a pass distance that can be set in the parameters.

Parameters

X
Length of the pocket to be machined.

Y
Width of the pocket to be machined.

Radius
Size of the fillet to be obtained at the corners of the rectangle.

NOTE

A value greater than the milling cutter radius must be entered in this field.

Pocket depth
Total depth of the pocket in the material.

Z Step
Indicates the maximum penetration step into the material. Depending on the pocket depth, the Z increment may decrease so that all passes are performed at the same depth.

Working distance
It indicates the lateral displacement between one pass and the parallel pass. It is recommended to set a pass distance equal to 60% of the milling cutter diameter to avoid movements over the corners.

Entry depth increment
Indicates the depth increment performed with one turn of the helix during the material entry procedure.

Working Speed
Indicates the programmed linear speed for machining. It is recommended to set a value suitable for the material, tool type and thickness to be cut.

Downward Speed
This speed is used during the entry procedure.

X and Y Axis Zeroing
Resets the origin of the X and Y axes at the lower-left point shown in the image.

The position is acquired by placing the center of the milling cutter at the indicated point.
For machines equipped with a “pointer laser”, positions can be acquired by referring to the point indicated by the laser itself.

Executing the machining operation

Enter the X, Y and R dimensions that define the shape of the rectangular pocket to be machined.
Verify that the tool data are correct, especially the diameter.

The following two execution modes are available

Pocket-to-workbench-position mode

To machine a pocket correctly, position the center of the machine at the pocket origin point, as shown in the figure in the previous chapter. This ensures that the entire machining operation develops correctly relative to the designated area.

Then set the characteristic dimensions of the pocket shape to be machined.

Before starting machining, it is essential to verify the accuracy of the selected tool data, paying particular attention to the diameter because it directly affects the precision and quality of the pocket.

The “workbench position” must be acquired with reference to the bottom level of the pocket. To determine it correctly, move to the upper surface of the material and zero the Z position. From there, move downward by the desired pocket depth. The workbench position can then be acquired using the dedicated button. When using milling-cutter tools, it is recommended to perform this operation with the A axis at 90_ to avoid inaccuracies due to the actual tool length.

Once the workbench position has been defined, zero the X and Y axes. This is done by pressing the relevant reset button and positioning the center of the milling cutter exactly at the point indicated in the figure by the reference symbol. On machines equipped with a pointer laser, the X and Y zero point can be acquired directly using the reference provided by the laser.

The pocket depth depends directly on the level set as the workbench position and on the Z-axis position when the cycle is started using the “Cycle Start” button. Machining begins with a helical entry at the center down to the depth specified by the “Z Step” parameter. The area is then cleared with a concentric movement, following the distance set in the machining parameters.

The machine movements required to reach the initial position take place at the so-called “clearance position”, which can be defined in the tool parameters. This ensures that the tool does not interfere with any obstacles during positioning movements.

Position-above-piece and origin-value zeroing mode

This mode requires setting and subsequently using the parameter: “Pocket depth”

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC2.6 CUTS

This function can be used to add multiple cuts.
This special type of cut makes it possible to create a series of parallel cuts within the same group, with the option of having two groups, each with its own configurable direction.
The interface appears similar to the following:

Sidebar

Cut-group selection and management

Create first cut group
Cuts are created parallel to the current machine position.
The direction in degrees for the first cut group is shown below the button.

Create second cut group
The second cut group is created in a similar way to the first, except that its direction may be different. The direction in degrees for the second cut group is shown below the button.

Cut management
In this mode, certain changes can be made to cuts before they are executed. Cuts can be edited, disabled, moved, deleted, and pauses can be added before a cut is executed.

Cut parameters

For each of the two cut groups available to the operator, up to 100 simultaneous cut configurations can be entered with their respective parameters.

Orthogonal directions
If the two cut groups have mutually orthogonal directions, the first green icon is displayed immediately below the cut-group selection and management buttons. Otherwise, the second red image is displayed.

Width

The distance between one cut and the next.

Numbers

The number of parallel cuts to create.

Cut position
These buttons are located next to each cut configuration and allow the operator to decide whether to position the cuts starting from the disk position toward the motor, or conversely to move away from the motor with the cuts.

Show next/previous cuts
Allows the operator to display all cuts in the selected group.
Editing the selected group returns to the first page of the group, where the first four cut configurations in the group are displayed.

Stretching Cuts

The operator can extend all cuts in both the first and second groups at the start or end by the set amount.

Start
This parameter can be used to extend the cut at its starting end.

End
This parameter can be used to extend the cut at its final end.

Delete and update cuts

Delete cuts
Clicking this button allows the operator to delete the created cuts and start again with a new arrangement.

Update cuts
When this button is pressed, the cuts are moved to the correct position relative to the machine.

C axis

The machine head can be rotated to adjust the orientation of cuts in both the first and second groups.

Rotate _90
Pressing the button rotates the machine head by 90_ from its current position.

Rotate -90
Pressing the button rotates the machine head by - 90_ from its current position.

Machine head rotation
The following parameter can be used to specify the machine head rotation angle (in degrees).

MDI
Pressing this button rotates the machine head according to the value set in the previous parameter.

Thickness

The operator can define the thickness of the slab to be cut.

Manual thickness
The operator can manually enter the slab thickness.

Thickness with machine
The operator can acquire the thickness using the machine by moving the machine height to the desired position and selecting the button. The distance between the workbench and the disk is used as the material thickness.

Executing the machining operation

The operator can configure both cut groups by changing their respective parameters.
Once the desired result has been obtained, the “Cycle Start” button can be pressed to perform the machining operation.

First cut group

In the first cut group, one or more sets of cuts are defined by changing the Width, Number and Cut Position parameters, as well as the C-axis rotation.
In the following job, the cuts have been set parallel to the current machine position.

Second cut group

As with the first cut group, the parameters of the second group can also be changed to obtain the desired result.
In this job, the direction of the cuts has been changed, creating several cuts orthogonal to those in the first group.

Cut optimization and management

In this section, the cut execution order can be changed and each cut can be enabled or disabled.

DOC2.7 ISOCAM

IsoCam is the software used to perform profiling operations with the disk; it allows shapes to be drawn or imported, the profile to be defined, and different machining methods to be applied.
Job programming is divided into several stages, which are described in the following paragraphs.

When the IsoCam program is opened, if no job has previously been created, the operator can create a new one starting from the first machining step.
If a job has already been created, it is loaded automatically and the operator is taken directly to the last step of the job:

Elements common to the various steps

The user interface consists of several areas.

  • Menu: quick utilities.

  • Top bar: functions specific to the active page.

  • Central area: contains the drawing or active area depending on the page.

  • Side bar: window containing the parameters to be edited.

  • Bottom bar: buttons generally applicable in different areas of the software.

NOTE

All these elements vary according to the operating context.

The following elements remain visible at all times, regardless of the current stage of the process.

Menu

The menu bar is located at the top, above all other elements of this interface.

Visible

The operator is provided with several settings relating to the visibility of pieces in the work area.

Options

Color-related settings can be changed.

Language

ISOCAM is currently available in the following languages:

  • German

  • English

  • Spanish

  • French

  • Italian

  • Portuguese

Right sidebar

Machine settings
Opens the settings panel in the center of the page.

INFO
Opens a small panel containing useful information and contact details.

Step Management
This section can be used to navigate forward and backward through the different workflow steps.

Close
Pressing the button closes the IsoCam program.

Machine settings

This panel allows you to switch to IsoCam Advanced mode, return to the basic version, and change the X and Y Grid Step values.

Bottom bar

New job
Opens a new empty IsoCam window, resetting the workflow to Step 1 of 4.

Working files
Allows a previously saved job to be opened.

Save job
Allows changes made to a job to be saved.

Edit job
Returns the workflow to Step 1 of 4, allowing changes to be applied to the job currently in use.

Section drawing (step 1 of 4)

The first programming stage consists of drawing the section to be machined. The window provides the typical commands of CAD software: line drawing, arc drawing, snap, move, etc.
The software is based on creating the section as a quick sketch, which is then edited entity by entity using the dedicated commands. Drawings in .dxf format generated by external CAD systems can always be imported.

Top bar

Line drawing command
Enables/Disables the line drawing command.
When enabled, creates a new line originating from the endpoint of the last inserted entity, if available; otherwise, the line is generated at the selected point.

Arc drawing command
Enables/Disables the arc drawing command.
When enabled, creates a new arc originating from the endpoint of the last inserted entity, if available; otherwise, the arc is generated starting from the selected point.

Moves the selected segments
After selecting an entity, pressing this button allows it to be moved within the work area.

After selecting an entity, this button can be used to flip it horizontally and/or vertically within the work area.

Fillet
After enabling the function, follow the parameters on the right

Reverse active selection
Reverses the active selection when the button is pressed

Delete selected segments
Deletes the selected entities

Right sidebar

Line properties

When a line is selected in the work area, the right-hand side column is updated to show the characteristics of the selected entity, which can be edited by the user:

Length

Indicates the linear distance between the two endpoints of the selected line, calculated from their coordinates in the workspace.

Corner

Indicates the orientation of the line relative to the horizontal axis of the reference system.

Δx

Indicates the change in the X coordinate between the starting and ending points of a line or entity, i.e. the horizontal distance traveled relative to the X axis of the reference system.

Δy

Indicates the change in the Y coordinate between the starting and ending points of a line or entity, i.e. the vertical distance traveled relative to the Y axis of the reference system.

Extend/Shorten selected line
Allows the selected line to be extended or shortened by a specified amount, changing its length while keeping the angle direction unchanged. The change is defined using the dedicated input field.

Round Angle
Automatically rounds the line angle to the nearest multiple of 90_ (0_, 90_, 180_, 270_), facilitating alignment with the orthogonal directions of the reference system.

Scale connected segments

Applies proportional scaling to all entities directly or indirectly connected to the selected line.
When this option is active while extending or shortening the line, spatial consistency between connected elements is maintained, preserving their relative positions in the preview.

Arc properties

When an arc is selected in the work area, the right-hand side column is updated to show the characteristics of the selected entity, which can be edited by the user.
The arc can be defined in different ways: by points, by center, radius and arc, etc.
The various characteristics are shown in the window that appears on the right.
Changes to certain characteristics can be accommodated in different ways, for example by changing the radius or the starting/ending point; the “Fixed center” flag is used to determine how the change is applied.

Changes the starting or ending angle so that the arc is tangent to the previous or next entity.

Determines the consequences of a change (radius or angle).

Translate / Move selection

When the “move” command is enabled, the movement parameters window appears. Movement can be performed directly by clicking in the drawing area (including with snaps active) or by setting the parameters.
The movement must be confirmed using the “OK” button.

Profile selection (step 2 of 4)

The previously drawn section must be applied to a suitable profile.
The profile can be linear or arc-shaped, in the X/Y plane or also vertical; depending on the selection, certain machining modes are enabled or disabled. For example, an arc profile in the XY plane can only be machined with a vertical disk, and vice versa for an arc profile in the XZ or YZ plane.
The profile type is selected using the buttons on the left; the parameters used to geometrically describe the profile are shown at the top center, and a preview of the result is shown at the bottom center.

Central area

Linear Profile

Set the direction and length.
The “Delta Z” value follows the sign of the Z axis (positive upward, negative downward).

Arc Profile

Define: direction, work plane, concavity and geometric characteristics.
Any change to the geometric characteristics affects other variables.

NOTE

The maximum radius that can be set is 9999mm

Circle Profile

Machined only externally with a horizontal disk.

Linear Profile parameters

Profile Execution

Two modes are available: “Along X” and “Along Y”.

Line length (L)

Horizontal length of the base of the inclined segment, measured between the starting point and the horizontally projected ending point.

End-point Delta Z (H)

Height of the inclined segment, i.e. the difference in position between the beginning and end of the segment.

Arc Profile parameters

Profile Execution

Choice between “Along X” or “Along Y”.

Choice between “XZ Plane” or “XY Plane”.

Machining type

Choice between “Concave” or “Convex”.

Length (L)

Horizontal distance between the two endpoints of the arc, i.e. the chord connecting the beginning and end of the arc.

Starting radius (R)

Distance from the center of the arc to a point on the arc itself. Determines the overall curvature of the arc.

Vertical rise (H)

Maximum height of the arc relative to chord L; represents the vertical distance between the highest point of the arc and the chord.

Angle width (A)

Central angle subtended by the arc, expressed in degrees.

NOTE

Changing any of the following values: “Length”, “Starting radius”, “Vertical rise” or “Angle width” causes the remaining parameters to be recalculated automatically.

Circle Profile parameters

Starting radius (R)

Determines the radius from the starting point.

This flag indicates whether the C axis rotates during machining (guard active) or remains stationary at C=0_ (guard not present).

Machining can be performed in two modes:

NOTE

Basic procedure

Step 1

To begin, press the "New job" button. Make sure the "Connected Segments" function is active, then enable the "line" command. Click repeatedly in the work area to draw the desired section. Once the drawing is complete, click the "line" command again to disable it. Then select each entity individually to check and, if necessary, edit its parameters.

Step 2

In this step, the operator can set some basic general parameters relating to the desired machining type.

Step 3

At this point, parameters relating to the tool, type, orientation and parameters of the selected machining operation can be set.
The “Machining parameters (advanced)” panel also provides an overview of all parameters set up to this point.

Step 4

A cut list for the current machining operation is generated automatically. Cuts can be inserted, edited and removed according to operating requirements.

DOC2.8 POLISHING (OPTIONAL)

The Polishing program allows polishing to be performed using different machining types. It is also possible to choose how the slab geometry is acquired: by detecting the points that define the surface vertices (from three up to a maximum of six), or by using a regular surface (rectangle) by entering the zero position and the values of the two sides.

Machining mode

To use this machining operation, first choose one of the two available modes by selecting the corresponding button:

NOTE

The ‘
Rectangle selection
’ and ‘
Free point selection
’ modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the other.

Switch to Free point selection mode
Pressing the button shown switches from the operating mode that uses a rectangle as the predefined shape to the mode in which the surface is acquired by selecting points.

Switch to Rectangular selection mode
Pressing the button shown switches from the operating mode in which the surface is acquired by selecting points to the mode that uses a rectangle as the predefined shape.

Entry/exit mode

The buttons shown allow the tool entry and exit to be changed between progressive and standard modes.

NOTE

The ‘
Progressive
’ and ‘
Standard
’ modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the other.

Switch to progressive mode
When this mode is enabled, at program start the machine moves from the working Z position to the safety Z position and then toward the first point of the surface to be polished (for a rectangle, the upper-left point). It then moves around the surface perimeter while progressively lowering the Z position so that, at the end of the path, the tool is at the working position. The machine then performs a polishing operation on the perimeter, after which the selected machining operations are performed in sequence. At the end of the work sequences, the machine performs a pass around the perimeter of the surface to be polished, then follows the same path while progressively rising in Z until it reaches the safety position at the end of the path.

Switch to standard mode
When this mode is enabled, at program start the machine moves from the working Z position to the safety Z position, then toward the first point of the surface to be polished (for a rectangle, the upper-left point). Keeping the X and Y axes stationary, it then lowers in Z to the working position, after which the selected polishing operations begin. At the end of the configured work sequences, the machine moves toward the first point of the surface to be polished and then rises in Z to the safety position.

Free point selection mode

This mode is displayed as follows:

Parameters

Point positions

Set
This button allows the coordinates of each point to be entered. Once the position has been acquired, the status of the adjacent figure changes from red to green.

NOTE

From a minimum of three to a maximum of six points can be entered.

Clear
This button deletes all saved positions if the settings are incorrect and the points need to be acquired again.

Machining types

Perimeter
The polishing operation affects only the perimeter area of the configured geometric shape.

Horizontal passes
Multiple horizontal passes are performed.

Vertical passes
Multiple vertical passes are performed.

Global repetition
The machining cycles can be restarted by entering the number of repetitions in the dedicated box. The box in the “Performed” column shows the number of repetitions completed for the entire machining operation.

Machining parameters

Steps

Each machining type can be repeated a fixed number of times using this dedicated field.
If the value is set to “0”, the machining operation in question is not performed.

Made

The number of repetitions performed is displayed.

Step [mm]

Indicates the distance between one pass and the next, selectable for each machining type.

Tool parameters for polishing

Working speed
Indicates the speed at which the machining operation is performed.

Downward speed
Indicates the desired speed when positioning along the Z axis at the selected coordinate.

Tool wear
Allows tool wear during machining to be taken into account by entering the compensation value.

Executing Free point selection mode

WARNING!

Between one machining operation and the next, the machine performs the movements without rising to the safety position.

The operator sets the position of a minimum of three and a maximum of six available points by moving the machine manually and using the relevant save controls. Once the points have been defined, the machining parameters are configured for each desired polishing type. The specific parameters of the tool to be used for polishing are also set.

At any time before the polishing cycle starts, the operator can change the tool entry and exit mode by selecting one of the two available options.

Once configuration is complete, the machine A axis must be tilted to 90_ and disk rotation started. The operator can then execute the programmed cycles by pressing the “Cycle Start” button. During execution, progress can be monitored in the “Performed” column, which shows the completed cycles for each selected polishing type.

Rectangular selection mode

This mode is displayed as follows:

Parameters

Rectangle position

Rectangle sides
The shape on which machining is performed is determined by the values assigned to Y and X, which correspond to the sides of the rectangle. The coordinates of the lower-left vertex of the rectangle are acquired using the corresponding reset buttons below each axis. Both values must be reset.

Machining parameters

Refer to the Free selection machining parameters mode for the following operations: Perimeter, Horizontal/vertical passes and Global repetition.

Zigzag
Zigzag passes are performed.

Tool parameters for polishing

Refer to Free point selection disk parameters for the disk parameters: Working speed, Downward speed and Disk wear.

Y-axis step for Zigzag
In zigzag polishing mode, the Y machining step can be changed, allowing the machining path to be divided into several passes. If the value is kept at zero or set to a value greater than the value assigned to parameter B, the polishing step along the Y axis is equal to the value of B.

Executing Rectangular selection mode

WARNING!

Between one machining operation and the next, the machine performs the movements without rising to the safety position.

The operator defines the position of the rectangle to be polished by manually moving the machine and changing the corresponding coordinate values. Once the rectangle has been defined, the machining parameters are configured for each desired polishing type. The specific parameters of the tool used for polishing are also set.

At any time before the polishing cycle starts, the operator can change the tool entry and exit mode by selecting one of the two available options.

Once configuration is complete, the machine A axis must be tilted to 90_ and disk rotation started. The operator can then execute the programmed cycles by pressing the “Cycle Start” button. During execution, progress can be monitored in the “Performed” column, which shows the completed cycles for each selected polishing type.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC2.9 PROGRAM LIST

The ISO File Program List page allows multiple programs previously created using CAD-CAM software to be executed consecutively, for machines with two work areas, Twin machines, or programs with multiple machining operations created while the machine is already running.

Top bar

The top bar displays information for monitoring the progress status of the list

Enable/Disable ISO Program List
This button, located at the top right of the ISO Program List panel, enables/disables the function.

List execution status
Indicates whether the list is currently running.

List progress bar
Shows the progress and execution status of the list.

List progress bar

This progress bar provides information on the execution status of the current ISO program while also giving an overview of the next program in the list and the program that has already completed machining and moved to unloading.

In the previous image, no program is yet shown as unloading because execution of the list has not started and no pieces have been processed. Conversely, if there is only one ISO file in the list or the job has been started and all other files have already been executed, the Next section will be empty.

During execution, program progress is displayed in real time, as shown below.

Side menu

On the right side of the suction cup panel there are several buttons for managing the individual files in the program list.

Execute next program
Moves directly to execution of the next program in the list.

Move selected item up
Moves the selected ISO file upward within the list of files to be executed.

Move selected item down
Moves the selected ISO file downward within the list of files to be executed.

Delete selected item
Removes the currently selected item from the list.
If multiple items are selected, only the first selected item is deleted.

Suction cup panel
Provides access to the suction cup management panel.

Suction Cup Panel

The suction cups can be used manually to move pieces from one work zone to another.

Suction cup buttons

Enable / disable suction cups
The screen shows the suction cup assembly viewed from above, divided into its various zones. Pressing the relevant area changes its status.
Green indicates that the zone is set for vacuum.
Red indicates that the zone is set for blowing.

SUCTION CUPS: RAISE - Suction cup parking
When the button is pressed, the suction cups are retracted to the rest/parking position.

SUCTION CUPS: LOWER - Prepare suction cups
When the button is pressed, the suction cups are lowered from the parking position to the limit stop. It is important that there is enough space for the suction cups to extend completely.

LIFT PIECE: RELEASE - Unload piece
When the button is pressed, the Z axis is lowered until the material contacts the work surface, the vacuum pump is switched off, and blowing is activated from all suction cups to release the piece. After a timeout, the axis is raised to the safety position.

LIFT PIECE: START - Lift piece
With this command, the suction cups are brought into contact with the material, the vacuum pump is switched on in the areas marked green and blowing is activated in the areas marked red; once the vacuum switch indicates that vacuum has been generated, the axis is raised to the position set for movements.

WARNING!

Pay attention to the active suction cups and use the largest possible area to lift the piece.

BLOW - Blow control
The button switches blowing on or off from suction cups that are not set for vacuum. The indicator shows whether blowing is on (green) or off (red).

VACUUM - Vacuum pump control
This button switches the vacuum pump on and off. The indicator shows whether the pump is on (green) or off (red).

Safety conditions

Pay particular attention to the active suction cups during lifting, ensuring that the areas used are sufficient to lift the piece being moved. Always try to use the largest available vacuum area to grip the piece and check that there are no defects or breaks in the material that could create hazards or machine operating problems.
Once the vacuum pump has been switched on, it may only be switched off using the automatic functions provided for this purpose. Pressing the reset button or the emergency stop mushroom has no effect on the vacuum pump, which will continue to operate. The pump can be forcibly switched off using the dedicated button on the “Additional Controls” page.
During automatic procedures, before lifting the piece, the vacuum status is checked by a dedicated sensor: if a sufficient vacuum value is not detected, the “vacuum missing” alarm appears. The pump will remain active until the vacuum switch detects a correct value or until it is disabled from the “Additional Controls” page.

WARNING!

Loss of power to the vacuum pump causes a rapid loss of vacuum and consequently causes the material lifted by the suction cups to fall.

Bottom bar

The lower part of the bar displays several functions relating to execution of the ISO program list, as well as monitoring of both the tool and the slab.

List execution management

At the bottom there are also two buttons relating to program execution modes:

Manual / automatic
Defines whether the machine status is manual or automatic.

Single / next automatic
Defines whether the next program will start automatically or not.

Slab and tool monitoring

At the center and right of the bottom bar, the operator can configure periodic tool diameter monitoring by setting checks at defined intervals based on the number of cycles performed.

Number of Cycles Between Disks' Probes
Specifies the number of cycles between one disk probing operation and the next.

Number of Cycles To The Next Probe
Indicates the number of cycles remaining before the next disk probing operation.

Tool diameter
Displays the disk diameter value.

Slab thickness
Displays the slab thickness.

ISO Program List Execution

If the ISO Program List is disabled, the switch at the top right of the panel appears off; the function can then be enabled simply by clicking this button.

The ISO program list is automatically expanded as ISO files are generated in Parametrix; however, the operator can reposition items within the list or remove them according to requirements.

Before executing the list, the operator can set the number of cycles to be performed between tool probing operations.
The number of cycles remaining until the next probing operation is then updated and displayed.

The operator starts execution of the program list by pressing the “Cycle Start” button. The programs are then executed sequentially, simultaneously displaying the current program, the program to be executed next, and the program already completed.

If the program execution mode is set to Manual and Single, list execution is interrupted at the end of the current program, immediately after the next program to be executed has been prepared.
In this case, the operator can press the Next button at the most appropriate time and proceed with execution by pressing the “Cycle Start” button again.

DOC3 PARAMETRIX

The system is designed to assist the operator in programming automatic cuts. The software can be used to:

  • Define the slab position in the machine work area and create the material perimeter for machining

  • Create pieces using parametric shapes

  • Import shapes created with other CAD systems

  • Generate a list of pieces to be machined

  • Find the best position for the pieces on the slab

  • Set special cutting functions

  • Program the cutting order and create the machine movements

  • Monitor cut execution on the screen

Work area and piece list

Below is a typical representation of the Parametrix work area with the imported piece list already populated and an acquired image of the slab.

List of inserted pieces

When a piece is created, the program adds it to the piece list; from the list, pieces can be inserted into the work area, some piece properties can be modified, and the number of pieces still required for the job can be checked.

Piece positioning

Parametrix allows pieces to be positioned within the machine work area to create the cutting file.
Once the slab has been acquired, the perimeter created and the pieces for the job created, the pieces must be imported inside the slab. Pressing the button in the piece table places the piece in the work area. It is possible to work with 1 or more pieces at the same time.

If the pieces are not completely inside the slab, a warning/danger symbol appears in the upper-left corner.
The appearance of this symbol indicates that problems may occur when managing the cuts; however, no program function is disabled.

DOC3.1.3.1 CREATING CUTS FROM DXF DRAWINGS

The machine can execute cuts, milling operations, and holes from drawings created with CAD software and saved in “.dxf“ format, with automatic recognition of certain workings to simplify and speed up the machine operator's work.

NOTE

For Parametrix to interpret this information, certain conventions must be followed when creating the drawing:
All drawn pieces must be closed and converted into polylines forming a polygon.
If a piece mark is to be added for identification, it must be placed inside the polygon.

Parametrix Settings for Recognizing Imported Layers

To access the window for customizing DXF file import settings, press the User Parameters button on the Parametrix top bar.
From here, go to the section dedicated to managing Layer names.

For each function type listed, the user can assign a name (corresponding to the Layer name set in the CAD software used) and assign certain parameters relating to the default values for some workings.

Function

Layer Name

Miter Cuts

Miter cut

Downstand

Downstand

Backsplash

Backsplash

Offset

Offset

Cuts under the material

below

Drip system

Drip

Milling

Milling

Rim

Rim

Drilling

Drilling

Additional Cut

Added

Anchoring hole

keil

Chamfer

Chamfer

Lower Chamfer

Lower Chamfer

Deactivate

Deactivate

Remove

Remove

Buttons

The buttons to the left of each working allow the operator to:

Information Window
Displays a graphical representation of the information required to create a Layer associated with the working.

Download Example
Downloads a DXF file containing an example Layer associated with the working.

Miter Cut Mode

To insert a miter cut automatically, certain conventions must be followed:

  • Miter cuts can be inserted only on piece sides; if the miter cut does not apply to the entire section, it can be divided into multiple parts.

  • A miter cut can be applied to external arcs (e.g. a circular table, or curved tops only as regards the external cut).

  • For internal arcs (e.g. curved tops), the cut is performed in steps; the cut is made by automatically inclining the disk, avoiding collision problems with the material.

For users of CAD systems, the procedure requires creating a Layer with the following properties:

Layer Name

Inclinato _ (followed by the number identifying the desired inclination angle).

NOTE

The inclination is expressed in degrees.

Example

Inclinato45 or Inclinato-45

When a negative value is entered, the inclination refers to a diverging cut; when the value is positive, the cut converges toward the inside of the polygon.

Downstand Mode

The downstand function is a working that creates a rectangular piece having the same length as the line set as the reference side.

To insert the cuts automatically when creating a downstand, create a Layer named “Alzata” and then enter the height value.

Layer Name

Alzata _ (followed by the downstand height).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimeters.

Example

Alzata100

This automation in Parametrix creates a new piece whose width equals the length of the line identifying the desired downstand side, with the two sides to be bonded together cut at the same inclination and ready for a miter-joint finish.
The inclination associated with these sides can be set using the adjacent parameter.

Degrees

Sets the inclination with which the inclined sides of the working are imported.

Backsplash Mode

The backsplash/downstand function is a working that creates a rectangular piece having the same length as the line set as the reference side.

Similarly, to insert the cuts automatically when creating a backsplash, create a Layer named “Rivestimento” and then enter the height value.

Layer Name

Rivestimento _ (followed by the backsplash height).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimeters.

Example

Rivestimento150

This automation in Parametrix creates a new piece whose width equals the length of the line identifying the desired backsplash side, without a miter cut and ready for a square-edge finish with edge gripping.

Offset Mode

The offset function is very useful when more material is to be left than the finished-piece dimensions; by drawing lines on the desired sides, the functions associated with the indicated sides are automatically shifted in the correct direction.

To automatically add the desired excess material, create a Layer named “Offset” and insert all lines corresponding to the sides where the setting should take effect automatically.

Layer Name

Offset _ (followed by the number identifying the offset measurement).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimeters.

Example

Offset3

Lower Cut Mode

The lower-cut function is valid only for machines equipped with the mechanical option that allows a cut to be made below the visible surface of the slab.

To insert a lower cut automatically, create a Layer named “Sotto” and insert a line representing the cut.

Layer Name

below

Example

below

NOTE

The resulting cut length also depends on the disk diameter and material thickness set in Parametrix.

Drip System Mode

The Drip System function inserts a cut with a width greater than the disk thickness and a depth less than the material thickness.

To insert a Drip System automatically, create a Layer named “Gocciola” and insert a line or arc representing the center of the width.

Layer Name

Gocciola _ (followed by the number identifying the Drip System width).

NOTE

The width is expressed in millimeters.

Example

Gocciola10

In this way, the Drip System depth is determined by the dedicated parameter.

Pocket

Depth of the cut associated with the Drip System. This value is not considered if the user sets a value in the DXF.

The cut depth can be managed automatically using the dedicated Parametrix parameter as the value, or the user can set a value by entering the “&” character followed by the desired thickness.

Layer Name

Gocciola _ (Drip System width) _ & _ (Drip System depth).

NOTE

The depth is expressed in millimeters.

Example

Gocciola10&5

NOTE

The resulting cut length also depends on the disk diameter and material thickness set in Parametrix.

NOTE

For curved Drip Systems, only one cut is made with the disk outside the arc itself.
Any parameters specified in the Layer name are not considered.

Milling Mode

To insert an automatic milling operation, certain conventions must be followed.

If a milling geometry involving one or more sides of the external polygon is created, the milling cutter performs the working outside the drawn perimeter; this also applies to a single side of the perimeter. If the working requires cutting the entire perimeter with the milling cutter, any disk cuts are removed.

The cut depth can be defined by creating a dedicated Layer.

Layer Name

Fresatura _ (followed by the number identifying the milling depth).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimeters.

Example

Fresatura10

If no depth value is specified in the “Fresatura“ Layer name, the thickness of the current working is used.

An additional function allows a polyline (open/closed, for example a circle or a single path composed of a linear polyline) to be inserted to mill a shape inside the larger perimeter.

Rim / Flush Top Mode

The rim/flush-top function is a working used to lower a perimeter, typically to recess appliances or sinks.

To insert the desired rim automatically, create a Layer named “Ribasso”.

Layer Name

Ribasso _ (followed by the number identifying the rim width).

NOTE

The width is expressed in millimeters.

Example

Ribasso20

In this way, the rim depth is determined by the dedicated parameter.

Pocket

Rim depth. This value is not considered if the user sets a value in the DXF.

The rim depth can be managed automatically by using the dedicated Parametrix parameter as the value, or a value can be set by the user by entering the “&” character followed by the desired thickness.

Layer Name

Ribasso _ (rim width) _ & _ (rim thickness).

NOTE

The thickness is expressed in millimeters.

Example

Ribasso20&3

NOTE

The fillet radius between the perimeter sides cannot be modified by the user; it is determined by the milling-cutter radius.

The rim can be performed on a closed path that does not overlap the piece sides; in this case, milling is performed inside the drawn perimeter.

Drilling Mode

The drilling function allows Parametrix to add drilling workings to pieces.

To insert a drilling working automatically, create a Layer named “Foratura” and draw a circle where the hole is to be made.

Layer Name

Foratura _ (followed by the number identifying the hole depth).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimeters.

Example

Foratura5

If the depth is not specified, the hole is applied using the material thickness currently used by Parametrix.

In basic mode, the radius of the circle corresponds to the radius of the tool currently set in Parametrix.

Additional Cut Mode

The additional-cut function allows Parametrix to add a cut.

To insert an additional cut automatically, create a Layer named “Aggiunto” and draw a new line over the line representing the side on which the additional cut is to be created.

Layer Name

Aggiunto _ (followed by the number identifying the distance at which the cut will be added).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimeters.

Example

Aggiunto50

The cut is added inside (where material is present) or outside (where there is no material) the piece, according to the sign of the distance:

  • If the distance sign is positive, the cut is added outside the piece

  • Otherwise, if the distance sign is negative, the cut is added inside the piece

When an additional cut is applied to internal cuts, for example those of a recess, the cut is added inside the piece where no material is present.

Anchoring Hole Mode

The anchoring-hole function allows Parametrix to add anchoring-hole workings to pieces.

To insert an anchoring-hole working automatically, create a Layer named “Keil” and draw a circle where the anchoring hole is to be made.

Layer Name

Keil _ (followed by the number identifying the anchoring-hole depth).

NOTE

The measurement is expressed in millimeters.

Example

Keil5

In basic mode, the radius of the circle corresponds to the radius of the tool currently set in Parametrix.

Chamfer Mode

The chamfer function allows Parametrix to add chamfer workings to pieces.

To insert a chamfer working automatically, create a Layer named “Smusso” and draw a new line over the line representing the side on which the additional cut is to be created.

Layer Name

Smusso _ (distance along X axis) _ & _ (distance along Y axis) _ & _ (inclination angle).

NOTE

The measurements are expressed in:
X: millimeters
Y: millimeters
A: degrees

Example

Smusso10&10&45

If the three values are not geometrically compatible with one another, the working is not applied.

Lower Chamfer Mode

The lower-chamfer function allows Parametrix to add chamfer workings to pieces.

To insert a lower-chamfer working automatically, create a Layer named “Becco” and draw a new line over the line representing the side on which the additional cut is to be created.

Layer Name

Becco _ (distance along X axis) _ & _ (distance along Y axis) _ & _ (inclination angle).

NOTE

The measurements are expressed in:
X: millimeters
Y: millimeters
A: degrees

Example

Becco10&10&45

If the three values are not geometrically compatible with one another, the working is not applied.

Deactivate Mode

The deactivate function allows Parametrix to deactivate cuts on pieces.

To insert a deactivate function automatically, create a Layer named “Deactivate” and draw a new line over the line representing the side to be deactivated.

Layer Name

Deactivate

Example

Deactivate

Remove Mode

The remove function allows Parametrix to remove cuts from pieces.

To insert a remove working automatically: create a Layer named “Remove” and draw a new line over the line representing the side to be removed.

Layer Name

Remove

Example

Remove

Hole Mode

The drilling function allows Parametrix to recognize any circle within the piece area whose radius is less than the “Maximum core drill radius” parameter.

Holes can be inserted freely in all Layers (except those identified as neutral).

An additional option related to the use of the core drill makes it possible to remove an island of material left attached after disk cutting. For Parametrix to consider this option, one or more circles must be drawn so that they intersect the sides of the island cut by the disk; using the “Automatic Hole Distance” parameter, a series of holes is then positioned automatically based on the material still to be cut after the disk cut.

Neutral Layer Management

If parts of the drawing in the DXF file are to be retained but not treated as cuts or other functions managed by Parametrix, they can be assigned to Layers recognized as neutral.

Create the Layers using the names assigned in the Neutral Layers (1,2,3) fields on the “Layer Names” page of the Parametrix user parameters. Note that the “*” character causes all imported Layers with the same name before and after the “*” symbol to be ignored during import.

Examples

WorkingDetails.dxf

VeinDirections.dxf

Top.dxf

Kitchen_WithLayout.dxf

Kitchen_Curve.dxf

BookMatch_Wall.dxf

BookMatch_Floor.dxf

Bathroom.dxf

DOC3.1.3.2 COLORING LAYERS

This function can be used to color one or more cuts of pieces created from DXF.

Buttons

Change Layer Color
Press the button on each row to change the color associated with the corresponding Layer.

Procedure

To associate a color with the cuts of a piece:

  • Create a Layer in the CAD software;

  • Assign it a color in the dedicated Parametrix panel;

  • Draw a line (or curve) over the line representing the cut to be colored within the Layer.

Once the piece is imported, the cut over which the line was drawn on the Color Layer will have the color set in Parametrix (not the color set in the DXF).

NOTE

The line drawn over the cut to be colored must completely overlap the line representing the cut.

Example

In this example, two cuts of the piece are to be colored. The “ColorE“ Layer was created and lines were added over those to be colored.

As can be seen in the Parametrix work area, the cuts take on the color associated with the Layer of the imported DXF file.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.1.3.3 DYNAMIC TAGS

This function allows configuration parameters to be assigned to Layers in DXF files.

Parameters

The parameters are:

Name

Used to define and identify the Layer name.

Entity Type

Defines the type of entities that will be displayed.

LineWeightMethod

Allows selection of the method used to obtain line thickness.

LineWeight

Defines the thickness of the lines belonging to the Layer.
This thickness is applied if LineWeightMethod is set to “ByConfiguration“ mode.
By default, Parametrix uses a line thickness of 2mm.

ColorMethod

Allows selection of the method used to obtain the Layer color.

Color

Defines the color of the entities belonging to the Layer.
This color is applied if ColorMethod is set to “ByConfiguration“ mode.

Buttons

The following buttons can be used to add or delete a configuration:

Create Configuration
Creates a parameter configuration for importing a Layer.

Delete Configuration
Deletes a parameter configuration for importing a Layer.

Example

In this example, the characteristics of the elements drawn on the “Veining“ Layer are to be modified.

The entities are imported according to the parameters set in the dedicated window.

DOC3.1.4 SUCTION CUPS

This section sets the speed for moving the piece with the suction cups.

Parameters

Speed XY

Determines the speed for moving the piece with the suction cups.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

Speed Z

Determines the speed for moving the piece with the suction cups in Z.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

Rotation speed

Determines the speed for rotating the piece with the suction cups.
This measurement is expressed in degrees per minute.

XY Unload speed

Determines the speed for moving the piece with the suction cups during piece unloading or lower cutting.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

Z Unload Speed

Determines the speed for moving the piece with the suction cups in Z during piece unloading or lower cutting.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

NOTE

XY unloading speed and Z unloading speed may be present or absent.
These choices are normally made when the program is installed and are determined according to the customer's machining requirements.
These options can be changed by contacting Donatoni Support.

DOC3.2 NEW JOB

This button completes the current job and starts programming the next one.

Execution procedure

A job is completed by generating the machine cutting program or by saving the state of the pieces.
This button can be used to clear the slab and pieces from the work area, leaving space for the next job.

A message appears asking for confirmation to proceed with creation of a new job.

WARNING!

Upon confirmation, the following are deleted:
slab photo and perimeter;
all pieces in the work area (including commercial pieces);

Parametrix keeps track of the pieces that have been programmed by updating their count in the piece list.
Pieces can no longer be added to the work area once they have reached the maximum number.

DOC3.3 TOOL PANEL

Tool type selection

Each tool type has a selected tool, as shown in the following example image:

The background of the “Disk” type appears light blue because it is the currently selected tool category.
Simply click the rectangle of the desired tool type to update the tool list below with the tools available for that type.
As a result of changing the tool type, it is automatically selected as shown in the previous example image.

List of available tools for selected tool type
