List elements

Tool type
Shows the tool type (disk, milling cutter, core drill).

Main tool information
The main tool information is displayed: name (top) and diameter (bottom).

Force Tool
Allows the operator to tell the program which tool is currently mounted on the machine.
It is used if the tool was changed manually.

Search filter

The bottom of the tool list contains a search bar consisting of the following elements:

The elements making up the search filter are described below:

Search by tool name button
If this button is pressed, search-by-tool-name mode is enabled and the search-by-diameter button is disabled.

Search by tool diameter button
If this button is pressed, search-by-diameter mode is enabled and the search-by-tool-name button is disabled.

Button to clear the applied filter
It becomes selectable only if a filter has previously been applied; pressing it clears the search bar text and restores the view containing all tools of the currently selected type.

Bottom bar

The bottom bar of the tool list provides functions for adding and removing tools from the list.

Add tool
This button can be used to create new tools; a dedicated window, shown below, opens.

Delete tool
This button can be used to delete the selected tool.

NOTE

The tool currently mounted on the machine (indicated by the green check mark) cannot be removed from the list.

Duplicate tool
Creates a new tool by duplicating the parameters of the currently selected tool.
The new tool has the same name as the previous one followed by the word “Copy”.

Add tool

This window is used to create a new tool. The required parameters change according to the type of tool to be created.
The following image shows the new-tool creation window for the available types:

Disk

Milling

Coredrill

Parameter list for selected tool

This list contains all parameters relating to the currently selected tool.
Whenever the currently selected tool changes, the operator can view the updated values for the desired tool and make changes to each value if required.
The parameter list and its values are also updated when a different tool type (Disk / Tools) is selected, showing the values of the selected tool for each category.

Disk parameters

The parameters associated with a disk are shown below.

Name
Name of the tool associated with the parameters currently displayed.

Diameter
Maximum tool diameter measurement.

Disk thickness
Disk thickness measurement, to be measured at the teeth.

CRF - Flange Rotation Center
Distance from the inner edge of the disk tooth to the C rotation axis.

Junction Quote
Safety position used by the machine when performing positioning movements during automatic programs.

RPM
Indicates the maximum spindle rotation speed in revolutions per minute.
This value is associated with 100% of the disk control potentiometer.

Internal water
Allows the use of internal water during machining to be enabled or disabled.

NOTE

For disk-type tools it is always disabled.

External water
Allows the use of internal water during machining to be enabled or disabled.

NOTE

For disk-type tools it is always enabled.

Disk rotation speed

The following button is located to the right of the RPM parameter:

RPM information
Displays the table with speed-to-RPM conversions.

This window displays a table containing conversions from rotation speed to RPM based on the diameter of the selected disk.
Recommended values for the selected disk are highlighted in green.

Milling cutter and core drill parameters

Parameters relating to tools such as milling cutters and core drills are shown below.

Tool length
Indicates the distance from the tool tip to a reference point.

Tool probing

If the machine is equipped with the optional tool-probing device, the procedure can be activated from this panel.
Starts a cycle that can calculate the diameter for a disk, or the length for milling cutters and core drills.

Buttons

One of the following buttons is located on the right side of the panel.

Start disk probing
Starts the probing cycle to measure the diameter of the mounted disk.

Start secondary-tool probing
Starts the probing cycle to measure the length of the mounted secondary tool.

NOTE

The disk probing button is available only in the “Disk” section of the panel.
The secondary-tool probing button is available only in the “Tools” section of the panel.

Procedure

To measure the diameter of the disk or the length of the core drill/milling cutter currently mounted on the machine, press the corresponding button in the right-hand section of the panel.
At the end of the cycle, the program automatically updates the value corresponding to the measured tool dimension.

Other buttons

The following button is located at the bottom left of the screen:

Switch to the “Slab machining parameters” panel
Pressing this button switches from the “Tool Panel” to the “Slab Parameters” panel.

DOC3.4 SLAB MACHINING PARAMETERS

When the “Slab Parameters” panel is opened, the machining-parameters screen is displayed, allowing the operator to manage data relating to the machining operation.
Machining data can be set and edited using the parameters panel.

Selected material management

At the top of the “slab machining parameters” panel there are several elements used to manage materials:

The elements making up this section of the slab machining parameters are described below

Selected Material
Displays the name of the currently selected material.

Create new material button
Pressing this button opens a window that allows a new material to be created.
The corresponding window is shown below.

Button open Materials Management panel
Pressing this button opens a window that allows the available materials to be managed.
The corresponding window is shown below.

Selected material thickness
The value in this field shows the thickness of the selected material.
This value is essential for all calculations performed by the program.

Add a new material

This small graphical window is used to compose the name of a new material:

If creation of the new material is confirmed, it is selected automatically.
The parameters and material thickness are updated accordingly.

Open materials management panel

This panel can be used to manage materials:

Search bar
The text bar immediately to the right of this icon can be used to apply search filters based on the names of available materials.

Remove filter
This button is enabled only after a filter has been applied; pressing it removes the applied filter.

Remove material
This button deletes a material from the list.
A material can be deleted only if it is not the material currently selected (this is visible and highlighted in the first image in this section).
An additional confirmation pop-up allows the material to be deleted.

Duplicate material
This button duplicates the material selected from the list and its related parameters.

Edit material
This button allows the parameters of the material selected from the list to be edited.

Machining type selection

The selection of the machining type controls the contents of the parameter-management window.

For each machining type, the corresponding preview shows the selected increment mode, forward cutting speed (plunge / entry speed for Hole machining type), and tool diameter.

Pass type

Full Pass
Full Pass performs the entire machining operation in a single pass. The tool therefore immediately enters the entire material and performs the machining operation.

Step Pass / spiral pass
These passes do not immediately enter the full depth of the material, but do so gradually.
This causes the machining operation to be performed several times at different heights until the workbench position (end of material) or the selected height is reached.

Machining types

Linear

Full pass

Step pass

Increment parameter description

Forward
Indicates the cutting depth in the material when the machine cuts in the direction of disk rotation.

Back
Indicates the cutting depth in the material during cutting in the direction opposite to the tool direction.

Last Step
Indicates the cutting depth required for the last tool pass on the material. This cut is always performed in the direction opposite to disk movement.

Speed parameter description

Plunge
Determines the speed during the tool penetration phase into the material.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

Forward
Indicates the desired speed for the forward cutting phase.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

Back
Indicates the desired speed for the return cutting phase.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

Last Step
Indicates the speed the machine must maintain during the cut on the last pass.
This measurement is expressed in millimeters per minute.

Acceleration cuts
If this parameter is set to a value greater than zero, the disk rotation speed is progressively increased from the start of the cut up to the desired distance.
The rest of the cut is then performed at full speed.

Slow down cuts
If this parameter is set to a value greater than zero, the disk rotation speed is progressively reduced starting at the set distance from the end of the cut, until the cut ends.

NOTE

For increments and speeds, the “Back” and “Last” parameters may both be present, neither may be present, or only one of the two may be present.
These choices are normally made when the program is installed and are determined according to the customer's machining requirements.
These options can be changed if a different machining method is preferred by contacting Donatoni Support.

Arc

Step pass

Miter cut

Full pass

Step pass

Increment parameter description

Cut with probing (enabled / disabled)
If enabled, before executing the miter cut the system performs two measurements with the slab probe at the ends of the desired cut and calculates the average.
This value is used during execution of the miter cut.

Milling

Full Pass

Step pass and spiral pass

Hole

Full pass

Step pass

Machining execution with step pass:

  • The machine approaches the material at maximum speed until it reaches the distance from the material specified in the APPROACH parameter.

  • The number of steps is calculated as:

    • Material thickness divided by step thickness

      • rounded up if necessary

  • The machine starts moving at machining speed.

    • If the ENTRY STEP parameter is set (non-zero and greater than zero), the machine works at the speed set in the second ENTRY field until it reaches the distance set in the ENTRY STEP field

  • The machine performs the steps calculated in the second point at the Step speed

  • After each step (including the first), the machine returns to the material position at maximum speed, then returns at maximum speed to a short distance before the start of the next step.

  • If the EXIT STEP parameter is set (non-zero and greater than zero), the machine works at the speed defined in the second STEP field until it reaches the distance defined in the first EXIT field

    • The remainder of the step is performed at EXIT speed

Description of Hole parameters with step pass

Approach position
The machine approaches the material at maximum speed until it reaches the distance from the material set in this parameter. From this point, the core drill begins moving at machining speed.

Step
These parameters define the thickness of the working steps and the machining speed. The number of working steps is also calculated based on the working-step thickness and material thickness.
For example, if the material thickness is 20 mm and the user sets the parameter to 3 mm, the hole is performed in 7 steps.

Way in
If this value is set to a value other than 0, an interval is defined starting from the first step and, if applicable, for subsequent steps, during which the machine works at a speed different from that defined in “STEP”.

Exit
If this value is set to a value other than 0, an interval is defined starting from the last step and, if applicable, for preceding steps, during which the machine works at a speed different from that defined in “STEP”.

Pause after
If this parameter is enabled, the machine pauses after each hole is drilled to allow the operator to check for any material residue trapped inside the tool.
The operator must press the START button again to allow the program to continue.

Change of cutting parameters

The previously described parameters for the disk, milling cutter and core drill can be changed if the user is authorized to use them.

To select the tool whose parameters are to be changed, press one of the buttons visible on the right side of the “Select tool” panel.

Change cutting parameters
Provides access to the screen for changing the cutting parameters of the selected tool.

Pressing this button displays a window containing a saved parameter configuration for each available material. The results also depend on the selected machining type.

The “Change Cutting Parameters” window opens, similar to the following example image:

At the lower left of the “Change Cutting Parameters” panel there is an initially empty text bar used to apply a search filter.
The button to the right of the bar is enabled only when text is present in the bar and a search filter is therefore applied. Pressing it clears the filter and empties the text bar.

Bottom bar

The bottom bar of the Slab Parameters panel appears similar to this:

This bar consists of the following elements:

Disk preview
Displays the disk tool currently mounted on the machine.

Milling cutter/hole preview
Displays the milling cutter or core drill tool currently mounted on the machine.

Tool Panel
Pressing this button provides direct access to the Tool Panel.

DOC3.5 ACCESS TO MANUAL CONTROLS

This panel provides access to certain manual machine controls.

Buttons

0_ - 90_
Rotates the C axis to 0 or 90 degrees.

Parking
The machine moves to the parking position.

SLAB PROBING
Any point on the slab can be selected; probing will be performed at that point.

CRF cycle
This button starts the CRF calculation procedure.

Washing cycle
Manually starts the washing cycle for a piece or the entire workbench.

Internal water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply through the inside of the tool.
The button color indicates the water status: White = Off; Blue = On.

Water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply from the main line.
The button color indicates the water status: White = Off; Blue = On.

Slab probing cycle

The probing cycle calculates the slab thickness and acquires the workbench position using the dedicated probe mounted on the machine.
To start it, enable the button in the manual controls panel, then press a point inside the slab in the work area.
A symbol is displayed at the selected position, indicating where probing must be performed.

Once the machine has completed the cycle, a panel opens showing several measurements obtained by probing the slab.

This information includes:

Thickness

Measured slab thickness.

Bench quote

Workbench position.

Slab quote

Position measured at the upper surface of the material placed on the workbench.

The data collected by the probing cycle can be saved using the buttons below:

Set slab thickness
Saves the slab thickness measured during the probing cycle.

Set bench quote
Sets the workbench position measured during the probing cycle.

Probing Start
Restarts the probing cycle at the same indicated position.

CRF (Flange Rotation Center) measurement cycle

The CRF cycle measures the distance between the inner edge of the tooth of the disk currently mounted on the machine and the C rotation axis.
To start it, enable the button in the manual controls panel, then press a point inside the slab in the work area.
A symbol is displayed at the selected position, indicating where the disk cuts used to measure the CRF must be performed.

WARNING!

During this cycle, cuts are made in the material.
The operator is therefore advised to pay attention to the slab position where the cycle is started to avoid damaging it.

The machine performs two parallel cuts with the A axis at 0_: the first with the C axis at 0_, the second with the C axis at 180_.
At the end of the procedure, the operator is asked to measure, using a tape measure or caliper, the internal distance between the two cuts on the slab.
This measurement must then be entered in field “A” of the panel that opens at the end of the cycle.

The measurements taken must be entered in the dedicated field:

To

Internal distance between the two cuts made on the slab during the cycle.

CRF (A/2)

Flange Rotation Center measurement for the disk. It is calculated as half the internal distance between the two cuts on the slab.

The data collected by the CRF measurement cycle can be saved using the following button:

Set CRF Measure
Sets the CRF measurement of the disk currently mounted on the machine to the value calculated by the CRF cycle.

DOC3.6 LASER MANAGEMENT

This panel allows laser references to be added to or removed from the work area.

Buttons

Line-laser reference
Adds the line-laser reference to the work area based on the machine position.

Draw cross laser
Adds the cross-laser reference to the work area based on the machine position.

Delete all drawings
All lines and crosses inserted in the work area in this mode are deleted.

Delete a single drawing
Allows the operator to delete a laser element drawn in the work area by clicking it.

Line laser

The line laser is a device aligned with the disk mounted on the machine. It is used to collect information relating to the position and orientation of the disk on the workbench.

To acquire the reference, move the machine to the desired point and press the button to detect the line-laser direction and add the reference to the work area.
Using multiple references, the perimeter and position of the slab or a piece on the workbench can be identified.

NOTE

There is no limit to the number of references that can be saved.

Cross laser

The cross laser is used to collect information relating to the position of the laser pointer on the workbench.

To acquire the reference, move the machine to the desired point and press the button to detect the cross-laser position and add the reference to the work area.
Using multiple references, the perimeter and position of the slab or a piece on the workbench can be identified.

NOTE

There is no limit to the number of references that can be saved.

DOC3.7 ADDING A PHOTO TO THE WORK AREA

This function allows a photo to be added to the work area.
If Parametrix is connected to a camera device, a photo of the slab on the workbench is taken.
Otherwise, the user is asked to select a photo from the computer files.

Take a photo

Generally, this function allows a photo of the machine workbench to be taken using the built-in camera device.
Pressing the button opens a window asking for the thickness of the slab that is about to be captured.

The photo is taken and then the panel opens allowing the operator to define the slab perimeter.

Choose a photo from computer files

This mode allows computers not connected to a camera device, usually located in an office, to insert photos from files into the program.
Pressing the button opens File Explorer so that a file can be selected for loading.

The user is then taken to the slab perimeter selection panel.

Perimeter selection

After selecting or taking the photo, this screen appears and the operator must define a perimeter within which pieces can be positioned.

Once the perimeter is confirmed, the slab photo is added to the Parametrix work area.

DOC3.8 SLAB PERIMETER

The program must know the edge of the slab to be machined in order to operate. This function allows the perimeter to be traced.

Perimeter creation mode

The program allows the operator to draw the perimeter using one of the following modes:

Rectangle mode
Allows rectangular perimeters to be created.

Point mode
Allows arbitrary polygonal shapes to be created.

NOTE

At any time while creating the perimeter, it is possible to switch from one mode to the other.
When switching from “point” mode to “rectangle” mode, the perimeter is converted into a rectangle and all polygon vertices are lost.
Confirmation is requested before proceeding with this operation.

Rectangle

This mode allows rectangular perimeters to be created.

To change the size and position of the rectangle, drag the yellow circles in the work area or edit the values shown in the bar below.

Measures

Perimeter dimensions along the X axis and Y axis.

Location

Coordinates of the lower-left vertex of the rectangle relative to the lower-left vertex of the workbench.

For points

This mode allows arbitrary polygonal shapes to be created.
To do this, the operator can place the points forming the perimeter at the desired positions as shown in the figure below.

In this mode, the perimeter can be managed using the following buttons:

Close perimeter
Once all required points have been acquired, pressing this button closes the perimeter.

Remove last point
If a closed perimeter needs to be edited, press this button to open the perimeter.
Continuing to press the button removes previously created points in reverse order.

Once closed, the perimeter turns blue and its vertices are indicated by yellow circles.
Both during creation and when a closed perimeter is present, the vertices can always be moved in the work area to improve accuracy.

Bottom bar

The operator can interact with a perimeter in the work area using the buttons in the lower section of the screen.

Snap to cross laser
Allows the operator to move perimeter vertices to the positions of any cross-laser marks in the work area.
When a vertex is dragged close to a cross-laser mark, it snaps to that position.

Move perimeter
Allows the selected perimeter to be moved to a new position by interacting with it in the work area.

Create a new perimeter

The program allows more than one perimeter to be created on which pieces can be arranged for machining.
It is also possible to define slab areas in which no piece may be placed.

Perimeter
Allows a perimeter to be created within which pieces can be inserted.

Avoid area
Defines the perimeter of an avoid area in which pieces cannot be placed.

Delete perimeter
Single-delete mode is enabled, allowing the operator to delete one or more created perimeters by clicking them.

Created perimeters are visible in the list at the top right. To edit a perimeter, simply select it in the work area or select the corresponding item in the list.
The currently selected perimeter has blue outlines and yellow vertices, while the others can also be distinguished by color: green for slab perimeters and orange for avoid areas.

NOTE

Two or more slab perimeters cannot overlap.

This screen can be used to add stress-relief cuts to the slab.

Slab heading
Allows stress-relief cuts to be added to the slab perimeter.

NOTE

Each created perimeter can have a different heading.

To complete perimeter creation, the operator is asked to enter some information about the machining operation to be performed.

Thickness

The operator must specify the thickness of the slab on the workbench.

Name

Name to assign to the slab job.

Customer

Specifies the name of the customer for whom the job is being performed. This field is optional.

Job

Specifies an identifier for the job. This field is optional.

NOTE

Slab thickness and job name are mandatory fields that must be entered before confirming the perimeter.
By contrast, the additional-property information below does not have to be completed.

Avoid areas

Avoid areas are zones of the slab that the operator does not want to make available for positioning pieces.
Reasons may include breaks in the material, unattractive veins, or the need to preserve certain parts of the slab.
They are represented as blue areas within the work area.

When the Nesting function is used, the pieces are arranged so that none of these areas is occupied.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.8.1 SLAB HEADING

Slab heading is a function that adds stress-relief cuts to the machining operation. These cuts trim the slab along its edges.
The function can be enabled in the perimeter creation panel.
The following example screen contains a diagram showing the four cuts, one per side, that can be inserted.

Sidebar

Slab heading
To add/remove a stress-relief cut on the slab, select the corresponding side.
The Offset value specifies the distance of the heading cut from the slab edge.

NOTE

Only slabs with a rectangular perimeter can be headed. The function does not work in “point” mode.
Multiple perimeters can also be headed differently.

Executing the machining operation

In the work area, the program checks that the operator does not position pieces outside the slab heading.
Pieces can also be snapped to these cuts, as shown in the figure.

During execution of the cutting program, the machine performs these trimming cuts before any other operation. Immediately afterward, a heading pause is performed to give the operator time to remove the discarded slab material.
In this way, subsequent slab movement operations using suction cups can be performed without interference from these trimming cuts.
These operations can also be seen in the list on the cut management and optimization screen.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.8.2 AUTOMATIC PERIMETER (OPTIONAL)

With this function, Parametrix can automatically determine the perimeter of a photographed slab.

Buttons

Automatic perimeter
Starts the calculation to automatically recognize the perimeter of the slab shown.

How to use automatic perimeter

To use this function, take a photo of a slab on the workbench or load an image from the computer.
The operator is then taken to the perimeter management panel.

In the right-hand section, press the button to calculate the automatic perimeter.

NOTE

Only one perimeter is calculated, assuming that the image contains a single slab.

When the operation is complete, the vertices of the calculated perimeter can be adjusted manually if they are not sufficiently accurate.

DOC3.8.3 EXTERNAL SOFTWARE INTEGRATION

The operator can integrate the photo system with different formats, for example Mapascan.

Execution

In addition to the image, additional files are often provided containing useful information relating to the slab, such as thickness, perimeter and other relevant geometric or physical data.

When the photo is opened, the data are analyzed to correctly set the perimeter, avoid areas and thickness:

Parametrix can read this file and import the slab photo, perimeter and slab thickness.

Multiple integration

When multiple integrations are configured, the one to use can be selected dynamically at execution time.

Window zoom

Show / Hide background color

Show / Hide piece names

Show / Hide right angles

Ruler

Horizontal

Vertical

X

DOC3.11 PIECE CREATION

Parametrix is designed to machine flat, closed geometric shapes representing pieces.

Piece creation modes

As can be seen from the top navigation bar,

pieces are created using one of the following modes:

Import DXF file
By importing files with the “.dxf” extension created using an external CAD program.

Create rectangles
By creating rectangular shapes and setting their width and height.

Create parametric shapes
By creating parametric shapes such as kitchen countertops, stairs, and other geometric shapes.

Import CSV file
By importing files with the “.csv” extension created using spreadsheet-management programs such as Microsoft Excel.

History
By re-importing previously created pieces.

Favorites
By importing pieces saved in a favorites list.

Create commercial pieces
By creating a large number of rectangular shapes whose width and height can be freely changed.

A more detailed description of how each mode works is provided in the corresponding paragraph of this chapter.

The selected function is highlighted in light green. When the “Create Pieces” panel is opened, the operator finds “Create rectangles” mode selected.

Import pieces into Parametrix

To correctly complete creation of one or more pieces, use the following button, which is available in every section of the panel:

Import pieces
Confirms creation of the displayed pieces and inserts them into the list of pieces to be machined.

NOTE

The operation of the piece list, located on the right side of the panel, is explained in the relevant chapter.

The following image shows how, after pressing the “Import pieces” button, the piece list is populated with the elements contained in the DXF file selected for import.

Imported piece list

The piece list displayed on the right side of the “Create Pieces” panel is initially empty. It is populated as pieces are created using the functions described earlier in this chapter.

Show Advanced Piece Information

Copy
Copies the advanced properties of a piece.

Paste
Fills the fields in the Piece window with the previously copied data.

View piece details

Following the example of the populated list shown on the right at the beginning of the chapter, the behavior of the following button is now highlighted:

Show piece details

Find source DXF

DOC3.11.1 IMPORTING DXF FILES

In this section, pieces can be created by importing DXF files.

File list

On the left side of the window, a list shows all folders and DXF files contained in the currently selected path.

The item at the top of the list

allows you to return to the parent folder of the current folder.

Initially, the list of DXF files in the PC working folder is shown. The folder can be changed using the dedicated buttons to the right of the file list.

USB memory
Provides access to the USB memory device inserted in the PC, allowing folders to be browsed and files displayed.

Working folder
Quick access to the PC working folder.

Browse folders
This button can be used to browse all folders on the PC.

Delete file
Switches to “Delete file” mode. In this mode, an eraser icon appears to the left of the name of each file in the list.
Selecting a file in this mode permanently deletes it.

Sort and filter displayed files

The elements below the list manage the application of filters and sorting of the displayed files.

At the top of the image there is a search bar that can be used to filter files by name, displaying only those containing the entered text.

This section of the screen also contains the following buttons:

Clear filter
Clears the text entered in the search bar, removing the file display filter.

Sort by date
Sorts the files in the list by creation date. By default, they are sorted from newest to oldest. Pressing the button again sorts the files from oldest to newest. The operation can be repeated several times to change the sorting order.

Sort by name
Sorts the files in the list by name. Press the button to choose whether the files are sorted in ascending or descending order.

NOTE

Search by name applies only to files contained in the folder and not to any subfolders.
By contrast, sorting by name and by date applies to every item in the list, while always showing folders before files.

Preview

When a file is selected, a preview of the drawing is displayed in the panel at the center of the screen so that its contents can be identified immediately.

The preview can be manipulated either by dragging its contents or by using the buttons to its right.

Zoom in
Increase preview zoom.

Decrease zoom
Decreases preview zoom.

Restore view
Restores the preview display to its initial state, with the entire drawing visible.

Additional buttons

The following buttons also allow additional actions to be performed.

Panel Details
Opens the panel for viewing details of the selected DXF file.

Panel Details

If a file has been selected, the “Details Panel” can be opened to view the DXF properties. This is done using the following button to the right of the preview:

Once opened, the following panel is displayed in addition to the list of pieces making up the selected DXF:

Layout visibility management

At the top of this panel, the layouts are shown as checkboxes that can be enabled or disabled as desired:

The first item in this layout list enables or disables display of all layouts.

Side panel

Visibility and padding buttons

In addition to the previously shown buttons for changing the zoom level and restoring it, there are two new buttons:

Highlight selected piece
Zooms in on the piece selected from the polyline list.

Pan view
Allows the preview to be moved by interacting with the screen.

Polyline list

On the center-right side of the panel, the pieces making up the selected DXF are shown as polylines.
Selecting one of the values in the list highlights the corresponding piece visible in the preview in yellow.

When the button next to each piece is pressed, the list of polylines making up the piece becomes visible.
A single DXF polyline can also be highlighted simply by selecting its corresponding row in the list:

Bottom buttons

These buttons are located at the bottom of the side bar.

Find previous open polyline
Moves through the list of open polylines in the selected DXF toward the beginning of the list.

Find previous open polyline
Moves through the list of open polylines in the selected DXF toward the end of the list.

DOC3.11.2 CREATING RECTANGLES

Rectangular pieces can be created by entering width and height dimensions and placing them in the list of pieces to be machined.

The program also allows an identifying mark (or label) to be associated with each piece and the number of repetitions of rectangles with the same dimensions to be set.

Parameter description

The following data are required to create rectangular pieces:

Number of pieces
Number of copies of the piece having the same dimensions.

Width
Rectangle width. It is measured using the unit of measurement shown to its right.

height
Rectangle height. It is measured using the unit of measurement shown to its right.

Mark
Label added to the piece to identify it. This parameter is optional because it is not essential for creating the piece.

Additional buttons

The following side buttons also allow additional actions to be performed.

Single import
If this button is enabled, multiple distinct pieces can be created as single quantities instead of one piece with multiple copies.

Dynamic Tag Top
Assigns the Dynamic Tag Top to one side of the rectangle.

To enable the function associated with each button, press it. It is then highlighted in light green.

NOTE

The “Dynamic Tag Top” buttons next to the width and height boxes are mutually exclusive. Therefore, the Dynamic Tag Top can be assigned to only one side of the rectangle.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.11.3 CREATING PARAMETRIC SHAPES

In this section, pieces can be constructed using parametric shapes with predefined geometry. To draw a shape, simply enter the values that define it.

Parametric shape categories

Referring to the image above, the main categories of parametric shapes are shown in the left-hand column.

Rectangular shapes
Such as rectangles and squares with and without internal breaks.

Quadrilaterals
Such as scalene trapezoids, also intended for kitchen countertops.

Triangular shapes
Such as regular and curved triangles.

Kitchen countertops
Various kitchen countertop shapes with internal cutouts.

Sector-type shapes
Such as circular sectors and partial annuli.

Elliptical shapes
Such as circles and ellipses.

Polygonal shapes
Such as regular and curved hexagons.

Bathrooms
Various curved shapes for bathrooms.

Stone or memorial shapes
Such as pentagons and Latin crosses.

Tables
Shapes such as rounded rectangles and irregular octagons.

Special shapes
Such as stars and arcs.

Preview and parameterized values

Depending on the selected category, the next column to the right displays the available shape selection.
An image in the center of the screen provides detailed guidance on the dimensions to be entered. To the right of the reference image, a preview of the shape being drawn is displayed and updates in real time whenever the values defining the shape are changed.
As in the previous paragraphs, once the dimensions have been entered, the mark (or label) displayed on the piece when it is inserted in the work area can be entered, the number of copies of the piece can be set, and single import can be selected.
The following image shows an example of creating a kitchen countertop.

Creating internal breaks

To create internal breaks, press one of the internal rectangles in the central image; the window shown below opens, where the break can be modified as desired and then inserted into the original image.

Additional settings

Additional parameters

The following data are required to create rectangular pieces:

Number of pieces
Number of copies of the piece having the same dimensions.

Mark
Label added to the piece to identify it. This parameter is optional because it is not essential for creating the piece.

Additional buttons

Single import
If this button is enabled, multiple distinct pieces can be created as single quantities instead of one piece with multiple copies.

Mirror
When enabled, these two buttons flip the piece vertically and horizontally respectively.

Reset
This button restores the shape being edited to its original state.

Out-of-square piece bar

Some pieces can be created using non-square angles (i.e. angles other than 90 degrees).
To use this option, a bar located above the central image contains all available modification versions for that image. Editable parameters are shown in green.

Mirror

Using the two dedicated buttons, the result displayed on screen can be flipped along the vertical or horizontal axis respectively. This function adapts the display to operating requirements or the type of machining in progress.

Some examples of horizontal and vertical flipping are shown below:

Horizontal flip only

DOC3.11.5 IMPORTED PIECE HISTORY

This function allows the operator to retrieve the history of created pieces.

Piece view types in history

Three different display modes are available for pieces in this section:

Cut view
The piece is displayed showing the cuts.

Dimension view
The piece is displayed showing the dimensions.

Bounding view
The piece is displayed showing its overall dimensions.

For the following examples, five pieces (A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5) were imported from the DXF named “Kitchen_Curve”.
Regardless of the selected view, all pieces can always be viewed both in the history list on the left and in the list of currently imported pieces on the right.

Cut view

The cut view highlights all cuts, both perimeter cuts and cuts inside the piece, while hiding other information such as their length values.

Cut-dimension view

The cut-dimension view highlights the external perimeter in black and places the corresponding length near the center of each cut on the perimeter.

Bounding view

The bounding view does not highlight any cut; instead it shows the maximum dimensions of the piece in terms of width and length.
In the following image, two black lines can be seen with the maximum piece length and width values centered on them. It is important to note that only by coincidence do the sides of piece A2 coincide with the black lines; the remaining cuts of the piece are not highlighted and show no information.

DOC3.11.7 CREATING COMMERCIAL PIECES

Commercial pieces can be created in this section of the “Create Pieces” panel. This type of piece has the following characteristics:

  • they are created with a high number of copies;

  • their width and height can be changed even after a piece is inserted into the work zone.

Parameters

Width
Rectangle width. It is measured using the unit of measurement shown to its right.

height
Rectangle height. It is measured using the unit of measurement shown to its right.

Mark
Label added to the piece to identify it. This parameter is optional because it is not essential for creating the piece.

Import a commercial piece

To correctly complete creation of a commercial piece, use the following button:

Import commercial pieces
Confirms creation of the commercial piece and inserts it into the list of pieces to be machined.

The creation procedure also updates both the commercial-piece list on the left and the list of pieces to be machined on the right. The following example shows both updated lists:

As can be seen in the column on the left side of the screen, a green icon precedes the piece name. Clicking this icon turns it red and removes the piece from the list on the right.

DOC3.12 PIECE LIST

When one or more pieces are created and imported into Parametrix, the program adds them to the piece list located in the right-hand section of the main screen.

Using the piece list, the operator can:

  • Insert pieces into the work area;

  • Keep track of machined pieces and pieces still to be machined;

  • Apply certain changes to the pieces.

List elements

Each row in the list represents a piece that has been imported into Parametrix.

As shown in this image, a row contains the following information about the piece:

Shape preview

Simplified representation of the piece geometry.

Piece mark

Label added to the piece to identify it.

NOTE

If the operator does not choose a mark during creation, the program identifies the piece using the name of the file (DXF or CSV) from which it was imported, or the side dimensions if it is a rectangle.

Number of inserted and total pieces

Indicates the number of pieces in that row that have been inserted into the work area and the total number of pieces of that type that can be inserted.

Insert pieces into the work area

To insert pieces into the work area, use the following button found on each row of the list:

Insert pieces into the work area
Inserts the selected piece into the work area.

The selected piece has been positioned in the work area and the number of inserted pieces in this row has been updated.

NOTE

Once the maximum number is reached, the “Insert pieces” button for that row disappears because all pieces in that row have been machined.

Operations on pieces in the list

The buttons below the list allow the list items to be managed. In particular:

Clear piece list
Deletes all contents of the piece list.

NOTE

Commercial pieces are not removed from the list.

WARNING!

All pieces linked to rows removed from the list are removed from the work area.

Hide/Show commercial pieces
Allows the rows in the list associated with commercial pieces to be hidden or displayed.

WARNING!

When rows associated with commercial jobs are hidden, all pieces linked to them in the work area are removed.

Delete piece
Allows individual pieces to be selected for deletion from the list.

Filter/Sort pieces
A filter can be applied to the pieces in the list, or they can be sorted according to different criteria.

Additional piece properties
The operator can assign and edit the additional properties of the selected piece.

Delete piece

This function allows pieces to be deleted from the list individually. After the button is pressed, the program asks the user to select the row to be deleted by replacing the arrow used to insert pieces into the work area with an eraser.

Pressing this button deletes the corresponding row and therefore all the pieces it represents.

WARNING!

Deleting a row removes all pieces linked to it from the work area.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.12.1 FILTERING AND SORTING PIECES IN THE LIST

This function allows the operator to filter and/or sort the pieces in the list.
Pressing the button opens the following window.

Filtered piece list

Once criteria for filtering or sorting the pieces have been set, they can be applied using the button at the top right.

Activate/Deactivate
Applies/removes the filter and/or sorting to the pieces in the list.

Pieces that do not meet the selected filter criteria are not shown in the piece list.

WARNING!

Pieces in the work area that do not meet the filter criteria are removed.


In the following example, only pieces with a height greater than 600 mm are to be shown and arranged in ascending alphabetical order.

Before applying the filter and sorting

After applying the filter and sorting

NOTE

The filter and sorting function does not work with commercial pieces.
Filter and sorting criteria are also observed by the Nesting function.

Filter pieces

In the upper section of this window, the operator can choose to add a filter based on various piece characteristics.

As shown, the following buttons are available.

“Exclusion” filter application mode
Pieces must simultaneously satisfy the last logical condition created and the result of the previous conditions.

“Inclusion” filter application mode
Pieces must satisfy at least one of the last logical condition created or the result of the previous conditions.

Add Filter
The created logical condition is added to the filter list.

Delete filters
Deletes all filters in the filter list.

How to create a filter

To create a filter, select the property to use from the options in the first drop-down menu on the left.

Once the discriminating characteristic has been selected, choose a relational operator from the second menu.

Then enter a value suitable for the property in the adjacent box to create a logical condition.

At this point, use the button to the right of the text box to decide how the filter being created interacts with other filters in the list, if any.

NOTE

In “Exclusion” mode, a piece must
simultaneously
satisfy the logical condition being created and the result of the previous conditions.
In “Inclusion” mode, a piece must satisfy the condition being created
or
the result of the previous conditions.

To complete filter creation, use the last button on this row. The filter is added to the list below.

Sort pieces

In the lower section of the window, the operator can choose to sort pieces based on certain properties.

After selecting an item from the drop-down menu, the following actions can be performed:

Ascending/Descending Sorting
The operator can choose to sort the pieces by a specific category in ascending or descending order.

Delete sorting
The operator can restore the original sorting by deleting the previously selected sorting rule.

Multiple sorting (Optional)

This function makes it possible to sort pieces in the list using more than one criterion.

In this mode, sorting criteria can be added using the following buttons:

Add sorting criterion
Button for adding a sorting criterion to the list.

Change position
Changes the position of the created sorting rules in the list.

NOTE

The criteria in this list are applied from top to bottom.
This means that pieces are sorted by the first criterion. If two or more pieces have the same value for the property linked to the first criterion, they are sorted by the next criterion, and so on for each criterion in the list.


The following image shows an example of multiple sorting.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.12.2 ADDITIONAL PIECE PROPERTIES

This function edits the additional properties of a piece. These are pieces of information about the piece that can be displayed in various parts of the program and are also transferred to the ISO file generated for the machine.
Pressing the button and then the desired row in the piece list opens the following window.

Property configuration

The central part of the panel lists the additional properties that can be assigned to a piece.

NOTE

The fields that appear in this window can be customized with the assistance of a Donatoni technician.

Buttons

The two buttons described below are located at the bottom of the window:

Copy
Copies the additional properties of a piece.

Paste
Fills the additional-property fields with previously copied data.

When confirmed, this information is associated with all pieces linked to the selected list row.

WARNING!

This panel can also be accessed by selecting a piece in the work area. In this case, however, the additional properties are assigned only to that piece.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.13 EDIT PIECE

This panel allows the operator to apply different types of machining operations to a designated piece.
When opened, the following screen is displayed:

WARNING!

Some of the functions described in this section are also available on the main Parametrix page, but with one difference.
If a piece or cut is edited through the ‘Edit Piece’ panel, all pieces in the selected row are modified accordingly with the same machining operations.
By contrast, if the machining operation is set from the work area, only the selected piece is modified.

Machining types

Using the “Edit Piece” panel, one or more of the following machining operations can be applied; each is described individually below. In particular, Parametrix allows you to:

Miter Cut
Change the inclination of cuts, both under-square and over-square.

Drip system
Add a drip system next to a cut.

Add
Add a cut parallel to one side of the piece.

Delete
Delete the piece cuts.

Offset
Change piece dimensions by applying offsets to its sides.

Hole
Add holes in the material, including to remove material the disk could not cut.

Milling
Replace disk machining operations with milling cuts.

Rim
Apply milling rims. Used, for example, to create sink recesses in kitchen countertops.

Lower Cut - (Optional)
Perform a cut on the lower surface of the piece using a dedicated mechanical option.

Downstand
Add upstands or recessed panels to the sides of the piece.

Curbs
Add a chamfered cut to one side of the piece.

Surface - (Optional)
Apply surface passes with vertical cuts and a horizontal disk.

Leveling - (Optional)
Apply a leveling cycle with vertical cuts and a horizontal disk.

Channel - (Optional)
Add a drainage channel to the piece using the disk.

Fillet
Round a vertex or side of the piece by applying a fillet.

Crop
Cut the piece using a side or a custom line as reference.

Internal break
Add an internal break to the piece, rectangular, circular, or elliptical in shape.

Drain board flutes
Create grooves by milling.

MaxBound - (Optional)
Determine the maximum bounding outline of the piece.

Mirror
Create a mirrored version of the piece.

NOTE

Depending on the combination of options, some of these buttons may not be present.

Cut list

The piece cuts are displayed in the lower-left section of this panel.

A dedicated division indicates whether a cut belongs to the external perimeter or to one of the internal perimeters. This classification allows the list of cuts belonging to a polygon to be shown/hidden by pressing the icon of the corresponding section.

As shown in the image, each row displays certain information about the cut it represents. In particular:

Manage machining operation
Button used to interact with the cut and apply the current machining operation.
On the main page, it enables/disables the cut.

Cut information

  • T - indicates the cut type (“Line”, “Curve”, “Milling”, etc.).

  • D - indicates the cut length.

  • I - indicates the cut inclination.

  • P - indicates the cut penetration.

Machining information

  • Machining type (“Linear”, “Arc”, “Miter”, etc.).

  • Pass mode (Full pass or Step pass).

  • Cut feed speed.

  • Diameter of the tool used for machining (Disk, Milling Cutter, etc.).

NOTE

This information changes according to the cut type it describes. Not all information is always shown.
For example, for holes only the penetration into the material can be displayed.

NOTE

If no cut is present on part of the piece, it is indicated by the label “None”.

Preview

The main area of the "Edit Piece" function provides the operator with a complete preview of the selected piece, showing all machining operations currently applied.

The displayed piece can be manipulated simply by moving the preview or using the zoom buttons located to its right.

In addition, this section contains other functions described below.

Mark
The mark of the selected piece can be changed.

Number of pieces
The number of machined pieces and the total number of pieces can be changed.

Add favorite
The piece shown in the preview is added to the favorites list together with all changes applied at the time it is added to favorites.

Cut selection

The operator can select a cut directly from the preview; its color changes to yellow to confirm selection. Alternatively, the corresponding row can be selected in the cut list available in the lower-left menu.

Clicking the green dot to the left of each list item disables the corresponding cut.
In this case, the dot turns red and the piece preview is updated, with the disabled cut changing to gray.
In the following example, the first two cuts of the external polygon of the piece have been disabled:

Bottom bar

This bar provides several functions that simplify use of the Edit Piece machining operations:

Cuts
Displays the piece cut list.
This is the default view of this panel.

Sides
This button displays the length of the Piece sides in the list instead of the cut length. Selecting directly on the image or in the list highlights the selected piece side in yellow.

NOTE

In this mode, machining operations cannot be added to the piece.

History
Displays the history of operations applied to the piece.
It also allows the piece to be reset to the desired operation.

Undo
Allows changes made to the piece to be undone.
Pressing this button multiple times allows the piece to be returned to its initial condition.

WARNING!

The button works as long as the “Edit Piece” panel remains open for the piece being examined.
If the panel is closed, the ability to undo changes to that piece is lost, even if the panel is opened again.

Edit view
Enables or disables certain piece entities to make the piece easier to view and edit.

History

Displays all changes applied to the current piece and, if necessary, allows the current piece to be restored to a previous state.
If changes have been applied to the current piece, they are displayed in the list on the left:

The left menu displays the processing states of the piece.

Machining state
Identifies a specific point in the processing of the piece. It displays:

  • Name of the current piece;

  • Date the machining operation was applied;

  • Name of the applied machining operation;

  • Icon identifying the machining operation performed.

The state of the current piece with no changes is called "Default".
Selecting an item from the left menu displays the preview corresponding to the time the machining operation was applied.

Pressing the confirm button restores the piece to the selected state. Changes made after the selected state are removed.

At the bottom of the panel there are three utility buttons for displaying the piece in the preview:

Show cuts
Displays the cuts on the shape.
This is the default active view.

Show dimensions
Displays the dimensions of each side of the shape.

Show angle
Displays an angle of the shape with its corresponding dimensions.

Edit View

This mode provides the operator with several buttons visible only while “edit view” is enabled.

Each of the following buttons enables or disables one of the following piece elements:

Cuts
Shows/hides disk cuts in the preview.

Holes
Shows/hides holes.

Milling operations
Shows/hides milling operations.

Rims
Shows/hides rims.

Arrows on cuts
Shows/hides arrows indicating the direction of disk cuts.

Piece name
Shows/hides the piece name.

Dynamic Tags
Shows/hides the piece Dynamic Tags.

Highlight Perimeter
Highlights the piece perimeter with a black line.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.13.1 MITER

The ‘Inclination’ function defines a machining operation with the A axis different from 0.
The interface for the “Miter Cut” machining type resembles the following image:

Mode

NOTE

Selecting one square direction excludes the other.

Positive square direction
When enabled, this mode allows the operator to create a miter cut with a positive number of degrees.

Negative square direction
When enabled, this mode allows the operator to create a miter cut with a negative number of degrees.

Parameters

Degrees

Represents the angle formed between the direction of the mounted tool and the surface of the material to be machined.
This angle determines the inclination at which the tool interacts with the material.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the desired cut.

Once the square direction has been selected, enter the desired value alongside it and select the cut on which the miter cut is to be set.
Applying the machining operation displays the miter cut in a different color.
Two distinct results can be obtained depending on the selected square direction:

Square direction: Positive

In the following example image, a miter-cut operation (45.0_) with positive square direction has been applied to every side except the internal arc, because the tool cannot be inclined inside the perimeter.

Square direction: Negative

In the example image shown, the miter-cut operations (45.0_) with negative square direction have been applied to the piece cuts in the opposite way to the configuration shown in the previous paragraph

DOC3.13.6 HOLE

This page can be used to create a single hole at a specific position or a series of holes at a fixed distance.

Machining types

To use this machining operation, first choose one of the two available modes by selecting the corresponding button:

NOTE

The 'Hole in the material' and 'Remove Disk's Material' modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the other.

Hole in the material
The operator can create holes based on coordinates.

Remove Disk's Material
Adds holes to the piece to remove material left by the disk.

Hole in the material

When this machining mode is selected, the currently selected vertex is highlighted in orange and a preview of the hole to be added is projected from it, also shown in orange and generated according to the set parameters.

Parameters

Penetration

Indicates the depth to be reached by the machining operation.

Distance X axis

Distance Y axis

Distance along the Y axis from the starting point of the selected cut at which the hole is created.

NOTE

Relative to the selected point, the area to the right of the circle is considered positive for X and the area above the circle positive for Y, as shown in the figure.

Executing Hole in the material

NOTE

A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the desired cut.

Once a vertex has been selected and the distance and penetration parameters set, the machining operation can be confirmed by pressing the green OK button.

Each hole successfully inserted in the material updates the preview and is automatically inserted in the 'Added Machining Operations' section on the left:

Unlike Remove Disk's Material, however, the center points of arcs can also be selected; these are highlighted in the preview together with all other valid reference points for inserting holes in the material.

Remove Disk's Material

When this mode is enabled, the selected vertex becomes the origin point of an orange preview consisting of multiple holes; their size depends on the mounted core drill and their number is determined by the Hole distance parameter.

Remove Disk's Material parameters

Penetration

Indicates the depth to be reached by the machining operation.

Automatic holes distance

Determines the distance between the hole origin points.

Executing Remove Disk's Material

Remove Disk's Material mode can be used between two consecutive cuts, regardless of whether both are straight lines, both curves, or one of each type.

DOC3.13.7 MILLING

The ‘Milling’ function creates a milling operation on the piece, on a side, on an edge, or around the entire perimeter.
The interface for this function resembles the following image:

Parameters

NOTE

One of the following modes must be selected

Corner

Removes material that the disk cannot remove without damaging the piece. It is used only to finish certain points of the piece.

Side

The milling cutter is used to cut one side of the piece. It does not run alongside the disk cut but replaces it completely.

Perimeter

Uses the milling cutter instead of the disk to perform the cut around an entire polygon of the piece. It replaces the disk as in Side mode.

NOTE

In every mode, the cut thickness is equal to the diameter of the mounted milling cutter. Changing this element automatically updates the cuts with the new dimension.
In Vertex mode, changing the material thickness or disk diameter causes the cut to be extended or shortened to adapt to the newly selected dimensions.
If the milling cutter is too large to cut the selected side, an error message is displayed.

Thickness

The slab thickness currently set in Parametrix is shown to help the operator apply the machining operation.

Penetration
Normally the penetration value is equal to the thickness; to change it manually, press the button shown on the left and the editable variable appears.

Milling on internal corners
Applies milling to internal corners.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the desired cut.

The effects of applying a milling operation vary according to the selected mode and have certain differences, described in the following paragraphs.
Milling starts from the approach point shown in the figure, identifiable by the filled colored circle positioned at the origin.

Each milling operation applied to a piece is inserted in the cut list associated with a polygon and represented graphically in light blue.

  • In Vertex mode, the milling operation is aligned with the selected vertex.

  • In Side and Perimeter modes, respectively one or all cuts of the polygon are replaced.

Execution on a vertex

The milling operation is applied to the vertex closest to the selected point of a cut in the preview.
It is applied between two consecutive cuts.

The following example image shows two vertex-milling operations: the first on an upper-left vertex of the internal polygon, the second on a vertex of the external polygon.

Execution on a side

Selecting any point of a cut in the preview applies the milling operation along the entire corresponding side.

The following image shows two side-milling operations: the first on the left side of the internal polygon, the second on a lower side of the external polygon.

Execution on the perimeter

Regardless of the selected point or cut, the milling operation is performed along the entire perimeter of the selected polygon.

DOC3.13.8 RIM

The ‘Rim’ function adds a profile to the upper edge of the piece or kitchen countertop.
It is mainly used to lower internal cutouts in kitchen countertops by a certain amount so that a sink can be fitted.
The tool used for this machining operation is the Milling Cutter.
The interface for this function resembles the following image:

Parameters

Plunge

The depth at which the cut is performed.
The plunge value cannot exceed the material thickness.

Distance

Specifies the desired distance relative to the side of the piece. Positive, negative and zero values are permitted.

  • A neutral value (0) creates a rim at the same level as the polygon cuts.

  • A positive value positions the rim inside the piece, creating additional adjacent rims if necessary.

  • A negative value positions the rim outside the piece, away from the polygon cuts.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the desired cut.

A rim is applied around the entire polygon of a selected cut, regardless of where it was selected.
Below is an example of a rim with a positive distance parameter value:

NOTE

If the rim distance is greater than the diameter of the milling cutter used for machining, multiple adjacent rim passes are performed.

DOC3.13.10 DOWNSTAND

This function creates a rectangular piece starting from the side of an object, thereby creating a downstand.

NOTE

This machining operation is available only on straight-line cuts.

Machining types

To use this machining operation, first choose one of the two available modes by selecting the corresponding button:

Backsplash Mode
Creates rectangular pieces with all straight sides.

Downstand Mode
In this mode, the two sides that are to be joined together are inclined by the same angle.

Parameters

height

Height of the downstand inserted during execution of the machining operation.
The width is predetermined by the selected cut.

Miter sides piece

If enabled, automatically inserts miter cuts where cuts would otherwise collide.

Additional downstand-mode parameter

Degrees

This parameter is active only when Backsplash mode is selected.
Specifies the gradient at which the machining operation is applied.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the desired cut.

Clicking directly on the cut in the preview, or where possible on the icon to the left of the cut in the corresponding list on the left, executes the selected machining operation.
Each downstand or fillet successfully applied to the material updates the preview and the cut list on the left.

Each piece created with this function is added to the Parametrix piece list.
The new pieces are also added to a list located immediately above the preview in the ‘Edit Piece’ panel;

This list can be used to select the desired piece in the block and display its preview and corresponding cuts in the cut list.

Executing Backsplash

The application of two backsplashes is now shown with the “Miter piece sides” parameter enabled or disabled.
A 1000 mm-high backsplash is first applied to the lower side of the rectangle, followed by a second backsplash on its right side.

Miter piece sides disabled

No inclined sides appear in the resulting shape and the cuts of the original piece are not changed in the cut list:

Miter piece sides enabled

If the vertices of the new pieces, i.e. Piece_1 and Piece_2, are aligned, the sides sharing a vertex and not adjacent to the original piece are replaced with miter cuts:

Executing Downstand

The application of two downstands is now shown with the “Miter piece sides” parameter enabled or disabled.
A 50 mm-high downstand is first applied to the lower side of the rectangle, followed by a second downstand on its right side.
In this mode, the original piece (Piece) and each generated piece (Piece_1 and Piece_2) automatically have miter cuts applied to all sides that are adjacent to one another.
The inclination angle is determined by the degrees parameter.

Miter piece sides disabled

In this case, adjacent sides between the original piece and the newly created pieces are automatically replaced with miter cuts.
The cut inclination depends on the set Degrees parameter.

Miter piece sides enabled

As in the previous case, miter cuts are inserted on cuts adjacent to the various pieces, and the inclination depends on the value of the Degrees parameter.
In addition, when the “Miter piece sides” parameter is enabled, as with backsplashes, if the new pieces have aligned vertices, the sides sharing a vertex and not adjacent to the original piece are automatically replaced with miter cuts.

Splitting pieces

When one or more pieces have been associated with the selected piece through Downstand or Backsplash machining operations, a specific button for managing the associated pieces appears at the top of the “Edit Piece” panel.

Split pieces
Button used to separate downstands and backsplashes from the original piece.

Before splitting, associated pieces are managed as a single unit within the work area. In this state, a block consisting of multiple elements is created; all undergo the same operations and have not yet been separated.

For example, when the original piece, a downstand or a backsplash is added to the work area from the piece list, all other associated elements are also inserted automatically.

When the Split Pieces button is pressed, each piece generated through downstand or backsplash is dissociated from the original piece and treated as an independent element.

Subsequently, both the associated-piece list previously visible above the preview in the Edit Piece panel and the piece-splitting button disappear from the interface.

NOTE

At the time of splitting, each piece retains the miter cuts obtained when it was generated through a downstand or backsplash, as well as all customizations and changes made while it was still associated with the original piece.

The following image shows independent management of the individual pieces that previously belonged to the same block.
In particular, only two of the three pieces were inserted into the work area (the original piece and the first piece generated by applying the first downstand), and the second piece was repositioned and rotated without causing any interference with the original piece:

WARNING

!
The piece-splitting operation cannot be undone once performed.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.13.11 EDGE PROFILE

This function adds a chamfer edge profile or a lower chamfer (bullnose) or both to the cuts of the selected piece.

Parameters

The ‘Chamfer’, ‘Lower Chamfer’, and ‘Chamfer and Lower Chamfer’ modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the others.

Chamfer

Lower Chamfer (bullnose)

Chamfer and Lower Chamfer

X Position

Y Position

NOTE

This parameter cannot be changed directly from the edge-profile section.

Perimeter

Enabling this parameter applies the machining operation to the entire piece perimeter.

NOTE

Square checkboxes, initially disabled, are located next to the first three geometric parameters. One must be enabled to specify which parameter is to remain constant; after a second value is provided, the third is calculated automatically. A checkbox cannot be enabled if the corresponding parameter value is zero, in order to prevent geometrically inconsistent or invalid configurations.

DOC3.13.12 SURFACE MACHINING (OPTIONAL)

This function allows the operator to machine the material surface.

Machining types

To use this machining operation, first choose one of the two available modes by selecting the corresponding button:

NOTE

The 'Rectangular surface' and 'Zigzag surface' modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the other.

Rectangular surface
The machine performs parallel passes to move across the surface.
The disk is used for this machining operation.

Zigzag surface
The machine performs zigzag passes to move across the surface.
The milling cutter is used for this machining operation.

Parameters

Axis C Rotation

Determines the machining orientation, which can be horizontal (0_) or vertical (90_) relative to the work plane.

NOTE

The '0_' and '90_' modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the other.

Pass Extension

Each cut generated by this machining operation is extended at both the start and end by the length specified by this parameter.

Depth cutting

Indicates the machining depth in the material.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the desired cut.

Executing Rectangular Surface

After setting the machining parameters, select a side of the piece on which to perform the machining operation.
The cuts are performed from bottom to top.

Executing ZigZag Surface

After setting the machining parameters, select a side of the piece on which to perform the machining operation.
The cuts are performed from bottom to top.


Slab machining parameters

The operator can change parameters relating to surface machining from the slab machining parameters panel.

Rectangular surface

This screen shows the machining parameters for “Rectangular surface” mode.

Parameter description

Distance between forward passes
Represents the distance between the forward pass and the next return pass.

Distance between return passes
Represents the distance between the return pass and the next forward pass.

Forward passes only
If enabled, all passes are performed in the forward direction, i.e. from left to right across the piece.

Return passes only
If enabled, all passes are performed in the return direction, i.e. from right to left across the piece.

Raise disk at end of pass
If enabled, the disk is raised at the end of each pass.

Piston pressure
Enables piston pressure on the material and allows its intensity to be set

NOTE

The parameters for passes in a specific direction are mutually exclusive.
If either is enabled, the program also forces disk raising at the end of each pass to be enabled.

Speed parameter description

Plunge
Determines the speed during the tool penetration phase into the material.

Forward
Indicates the desired speed for the forward cutting phase.

Back
Indicates the desired speed for the return cutting phase.

Zigzag surface

This screen shows the machining parameters for “Zigzag surface” mode.

Parameter description

Distance between forward passes
Represents the vertical distance between the starting point of the diagonal pass and its ending point in the forward direction.

Distance between return passes
Represents the vertical distance between the starting point of the diagonal pass and its ending point in the return direction.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.13.13 LEVELING (OPTIONAL)

This function allows the operator to level the piece.

Parameters

Pass Extension

Each cut generated by this machining operation is extended at both the start and end by the length specified by this parameter.

Executing the machining operation

Starting from the slab thickness set in the material parameters, the piece is machined as follows to reach the target thickness set in the machining parameters:

  1. First, parallel cuts are performed from left to right at a distance set in the parameters, using the linear-cut parameters.

  2. Then cuts are performed along the Y axis to create a grid, again using the linear-cut parameters.

WARNING!

The initial slab thickness must be set as the material thickness (probing can then be added for greater accuracy).
The target thickness is set in the machining parameters (and is referenced to the workbench position).

NOTE

The following machining operation can also be performed on commercial pieces.

Slab machining parameters

The operator can change leveling-related parameters from the slab machining parameters panel.

Leveling cut parameters

Parameter description

Distance between horizontal passes
Represents the distance between two parallel passes in the horizontal direction.
The button selects whether the passes are performed from top to bottom or vice versa.

Distance between vertical passes
Represents the distance between two parallel passes in the vertical direction.
The button selects whether the passes are performed from left to right or vice versa.

Leveling position
Sets the thickness the material must have after leveling.

Rotate tool 90 degrees
If enabled, leveling is performed with the A axis at 90_.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.13.14 CHANNELS (OPTIONAL)

This function allows the operator to add a channel to an area of the piece.
The interface for this function resembles the following image:

Parameters

Distance from cut

The operator must enter the desired distance in mm from one of the piece edges.
If the channel is to be flush with the edge, leave the value at 0; otherwise, enter the desired distance.

Cut thickness

The operator must enter the channel machining width in mm.

Cutting depth

The operator must enter the channel machining depth in mm.

Start Distance

The operator can enter the distance in mm from the channel reference cut.

End Distance

The operator can enter the distance in mm from the piece reference cut for the channel.

Automatic drip systems

The operator can choose whether drip systems are created automatically on the piece after the channel has been created.

Thickness

Material thickness.

NOTE

Start distance, end distance and automatic drip systems can be enabled or disabled using the buttons to the right of the value.
When disabled, Parametrix ignores them; when enabled, the program calculates the displacement.

Executing the machining operation

Channel with start and end distances disabled

The channel is created at a distance of 250mm from the selected cut and extends along the entire length of the piece, with a machining width of 100mm and a cutting depth of 10mm.

Channel with start distance enabled and end distance disabled

The channel is created at a distance of 250mm from the selected cut, with a machining width of 100mm and a cutting depth of 10mm.

As can be seen, with a start distance of 100mm, the channel starts 100m from the selected cut.

Channel with start distance disabled and end distance enabled

The channel is created at a distance of 250mm from the selected cut, with a machining width of 100mm and a cutting depth of 10mm.

As can be seen, with an end distance of 100mm, the channel ends 100m from the selected cut.

Channel with start and end distances enabled

The channel is created at a distance of 250mm from the selected cut, with a machining width of 100mm and a cutting depth of 10mm.

As can be seen, with a start distance of 100mm and an end distance of 100mm, the channel starts and ends 100m from the selected cut.

Channel with automatic drip systems enabled

Drip systems are automatically added to the piece (for drip systems see chapter 3.12.2).

The drip systems are positioned halfway between the channel and the nearest cut.

Z quote work start
Sets the position the machine must maintain while it is not performing cuts.

Offset work

Arc step

Probe check
Determines whether or not to perform a verification probe before machining.

Forward
