DOC3.13.15 FILLET

This function allows the operator to add a fillet to a vertex or side of the piece.
The interface for this function resembles the following image:

Parameters

NOTE

The ‘Single vertex’, ‘Side’ and ‘Polygon vertices’ modes are mutually exclusive: enabling one automatically disables the others.

Single vertex
Applies a single fillet to the selected vertex.

Side
A fillet is added to the selected side.

Polygon vertices
In this mode, fillets are added to all vertices of the selected polygon.

Parameters for ‘Single vertex’ and ‘Polygon vertices’

Radius R
Fillet radius.

‘Side’ parameters

Offset 0
Measures how much to widen the piece on the selected side, i.e. the side on which the fillet is performed.
The movement is inward if the value is negative, or outward if it is positive.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the desired cut.

The application of fillets in the different modes is shown below. A machining preview allows the operator to view the expected result. The machining operation is actually applied only after confirmation using the green 'OK' button.

WARNING

!
Each time a fillet is applied, all settings previously applied to the piece cuts are lost.

Executing fillet on a single vertex

When this mode is selected, the machining operation can be performed on individual vertices of the piece.
For the machining operation to be applied correctly, the radius parameter cannot be set to a negative value.

In the following example image, three fillets with a radius of 100,0 mm have been applied.

The cut list on the left shows several consequences each time a fillet is applied to a vertex:

  • If other machining operations are present, they are removed.

  • A curve is inserted in the list: the new fillet.

  • The lengths of the sides adjacent to the selected vertex are reduced by the amount specified by the Radius parameter.

Executing fillet on a side

When this mode is selected, the machining operation can be performed on the sides of the piece. In this mode, there are two main cases for fillets depending on the value of the offset parameter: a positive value and a negative value.

In the following example image, a fillet has been applied to the lower cut of the selected piece, with the offset parameter set to 100,0 mm.

The following image shows the opposite example: a fillet has been applied to the lower cut of the selected piece with the offset parameter set to a negative value of -100mm.

The cut list on the left shows several consequences each time a fillet is applied to a side:

  • If other machining operations are present, they are removed.

  • The selected straight-line cut is replaced by a curved cut.

    • With a positive offset parameter value, the inserted fillet consists of a curve recessed relative to the selected polygon, whether internal or external.

    • By contrast, with a negative offset value, the applied fillet consists of a curve protruding relative to the selected polygon.

Executing fillet on the vertices of the selected polygon

This mode applies as many fillets as there are vertices in the selected polygon.
For the machining operation to succeed, a negative radius value cannot be entered.
The following image shows the machining operation on all vertices of the piece:

As with single-vertex mode, using this mode has several consequences in the cut list on the left:

  • If other machining operations are present, they are removed.

  • The selected straight-line cut is replaced by a curved cut.

    • With a positive offset parameter value, the inserted fillet consists of a curve recessed relative to the selected polygon, whether internal or external.

    • By contrast, with a negative offset value, the applied fillet consists of a curve protruding relative to the selected polygon.

DOC3.13.16 SPLIT

The ‘Split’ function cuts the piece using a reference, side, perpendicular line or custom line.
The interface for this function resembles the following image:

Parameters

To use this machining operation, first choose one of the three available modes by selecting the corresponding button:

Parallel cut
When this mode is selected, the splitting cut is performed along the longitudinal axis of the selected side.

Orthogonal cut
When this mode is selected, the splitting cut is performed obliquely relative to the selected side, with its origin point coinciding with the center of that side.

Cut through two points
When this mode is selected, the splitting cut is defined by manually specifying the coordinates of the two endpoints that determine the separation line between the pieces.

Parameters for ‘Parallel cut’ and ‘Orthogonal cut’

For the next two buttons below, this function can be enabled or disabled by clicking the checkbox to the right of the ‘Cut extension’ label.

Stretching Cuts

This function allows the operator to extend the cut applied to the selected side, extending it to cover the entire length of the piece in the cutting direction.

Offset

The operator can set the cut distance along the transverse axis, measured relative to the center of the reference side.

Parameters for 'Cut Through Two Points'

For the next button, the coordinates of the two points that define the dividing line can be specified.

Setting Dividing Line Point Parameters

When the function is activated, four parameter fields are available in which the operator can specify the coordinates (X, Y) of the start and end points of the cutting line.

Cut Orientation
By pressing the dedicated command, the user can choose the cut orientation—horizontal, vertical, or free—relative to the starting point of the previously defined line.

Vertex Snap
When free cutting is selected in the previous parameter, an additional parameter appears to its right which, when activated, makes it easier to snap to the figure vertices when defining the cutting-line points.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the desired cut.

Parallel cut

In the following image, a parallel cut has been performed on the piece already shown on the chapter cover:

Orthogonal cut

In the following image, an orthogonal cut has been performed on the piece already shown on the chapter cover:

Cut through two points

In the following image, a cut through two points has been performed using the vertex snap function on the piece already shown on the chapter cover:

In the following image, a cut through two points has been performed without using any special function on the piece already shown on the chapter cover:

Splitting pieces

When one or more pieces have been associated with the selected piece through Split workings, a specific button for managing the associated pieces appears at the top of the “Edit Piece” panel.

Split pieces
Button used to separate the split pieces from the original piece.

Before splitting, associated pieces are managed as a single unit within the work area. In this state, a block consisting of multiple elements is created; all undergo the same operations and have not yet been separated.

For example, when one of the pieces generated through split is added to the work area from the piece list, all the other associated elements are also added automatically.

When the Split Pieces button is pressed, each piece generated through split is disassociated from the original piece and treated as an independent element.

Subsequently, both the associated-piece list previously visible above the preview in the Edit Piece panel and the piece-splitting button disappear from the interface.

WARNING

!
The piece-splitting operation cannot be undone once performed.

DOC3.13.17 INTERNAL BREAK

The 'Internal Break' function allows an internal rectangular, circular, or elliptical recess to be added to the piece.
The interface for this function resembles the following image:

Machining types

To use this machining operation, first choose one of the two available modes by selecting the corresponding button:

NOTE

The 'Rectangular', 'Circular', and 'Elliptical' modes are mutually exclusive: activating one automatically disables the others.

Rectangular Break
Selecting this mode provides access to the configuration of specific parameters required to execute a rectangular break working.

Circular Break
Selecting this mode provides access to the configuration of specific parameters required to execute a circular break working.

Elliptical Break
Selecting this mode provides access to the configuration of specific parameters required to execute an elliptical break working.

Rectangular Break

When this mode is activated, a preview of the rectangular break is displayed directly in the working preview, highlighted in light green. The dimensions and position of the break depend on the default parameters, which can be modified by the user.

Rectangular Break Parameters

While in this mode, the following parameter panel is displayed:

Offset O

Distance between the edge of the break and the reference side of the selected piece.

Midpoint offset D

Distance between the side of the piece parallel to the selected side and the center of the break.

NOTE

For curved cuts, the central offset D can be specified in mm or degrees using a button.

Height H

Break height.

Width W

Break width.

Executing a Rectangular Break

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the desired cut.

Confirming the working adds a new internal polygon to the piece, both graphically and in the polygon list on the left:

Circular Break

When this mode is activated, a preview of the circular break is displayed directly in the working preview, highlighted in light green. The dimensions and position of the break depend on the default parameters, which can be modified by the user.

Circular Break Parameters

While in this mode, the following parameter panel is displayed:

Offset O

Distance between the edge of the break and the reference side of the selected piece.

Midpoint offset D

Distance between the side of the piece parallel to the selected side and the center of the break.

NOTE

For curved cuts, the central offset D can be specified in mm or degrees using a small button.

Radius R

Break radius.

Executing a Circular Break

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the desired cut.

Confirming the working adds a new internal polygon to the piece, both graphically and in the polygon list on the left:

Elliptical Break

When this mode is activated, a preview of the elliptical break is displayed directly in the working preview, highlighted in light green. The dimensions and position of the break depend on the default parameters, which can be modified by the user.

Elliptical Break Parameters

While in this mode, the following parameter panel is displayed:

Offset O

Distance between the edge of the break and the reference side of the selected piece.

Midpoint offset D

Distance between the side of the piece parallel to the selected side and the center of the break.

NOTE

For curved cuts, the central offset D can be specified in mm or degrees using a button.

To

Value corresponding to the semi-major axis of the elliptical break.

B

Value corresponding to the semi-minor axis of the elliptical break.

Executing an Elliptical Break

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the desired cut.

Confirming the working adds a new internal polygon to the piece, both graphically and in the polygon list on the left:

Optional Tap Holes

Pressing the button to the left of the OK button activates the tap-hole option. This option creates additional holes around the main central hole and displays additional parameters to configure.

NOTE

If the tap-hole diameter is equal to or less than the maximum hole radius value, the tap holes are created as holes; if the tap-hole diameter is greater than the maximum hole radius value, the tap holes are created as internal interruptions.

Tap Hole Parameters

While in this mode, the following parameter panel is displayed:

Holes number

Indicates how many holes to apply to the current working on the selected cut.

Hole Diameter

Indicates the diameter of the holes applied to the working.

Distance Between Holes

Indicates the distance measured between the centers of two consecutive holes.

Distance from Break

Indicates the distance between the center of the hole and the edge of the break.

Executing Tap Holes

NOTE
The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.

DOC3.13.18 FLUTES

This function allows workings to be applied to the selected cut, whether curved or straight, using the milling-cutter tool currently mounted on the machine in order to create flutes.

Parameters

The result varies according to the value of the following parameters:

Number of drain board flutes

Indicates how many flutes to apply to the current working on the selected cut.

NOTE

This parameter is visible only when the number-based flute insertion mode is selected.

Recalculate Number
Recalculates the number of flutes so as to fill the selected cut.

NOTE

This parameter is visible only when the number-based flute insertion mode is selected.

Length

Indicates how far the flutes extend into the cut.

Distance

This value represents the distance between the flutes and takes into account the diameter of the mounted tool.

Start Distance

This value defines the distance between the vertices of the flutes inside the piece, adjusting the empty space separating them.

Internal extension

Indicates how far the flutes will be extended beyond the reference cut.

Start depth

Penetration into the material at the starting point of the drain-board flute.

Final depth

Penetration into the material at the ending point of the drain-board flute.

Flute Type on Arcs

For flutes on curves, three modes are available as described below.

NOTE

This parameter is visible only when a curved cut is selected.

Cut Thickness

For flutes inserted in disk mode, the cut-thickness variable is available.

NOTE

This parameter is visible only when disk mode is selected to insert the flutes.

Overlay on Drip System

For flutes inserted in fill mode, the percentage can be modified.

NOTE

This parameter is visible only when fill mode is selected to insert the flutes.

Recalculate Number

Pressing the button to the right of the number of flutes fills the selected cut with as many flutes as possible, according to the values of the other parameters.
The following example image shows the result of flute filling, in contrast with the first image at the beginning of the chapter.

Flute Insertion Mode

These are the flute insertion options:

Number-Based Insertion
The flutes are inserted according to the entered number.

NOTE

If this insertion mode is selected, fill insertion cannot be used, and vice versa.

Fill Insertion
The flutes are inserted according to the entered distance.

Disk Mode
The disk will be used to cut the flutes.

NOTE

If this mode is selected, milling-cutter mode cannot be used, and vice versa.

Milling Cutter Mode
The milling cutter will be used to cut the flutes.

Flute Mode on Arcs

When a curved cut of a polygon is selected, a new parameter is displayed and can take one of three values:

Radial
The flutes are arranged along the curve so that they point toward the center of the arc.

Arc Alignment
The flutes are arranged parallel along the curve and with equal length.

Tangent Alignment
The flutes are arranged parallel along the curve. Their length varies so that all ends inside the piece lie on the same straight line, while respecting the extension of the ends outside the piece.

Mode 1: Radial

In this mode, the flutes share a common origin point and are perpendicular to the corresponding tangent on the selected curved cut.

Mode 2: Arc Alignment

In this mode, the flutes are parallel to each other and aligned along the arc both for spacing and internal extension.

Mode 3: Tangent Alignment

In this mode, the flutes are parallel to each other and arc-aligned for the internal extension, while they are extended until they reach the tangent at the distance specified by the length value.

Executing the machining operation

NOTE

The machining operation can be applied by pressing the button to the left of the appropriate cut in the polygon list.
A red icon with an 'X' indicates that the machining operation cannot be applied to the desired cut.

Once the desired result has been obtained, displayed and continuously updated in the working preview, the operator can confirm the operation by pressing the green “OK” button located just below the set parameters.
The flutes shown in the preview are then applied to the selected cut: their color changes to dark green, both in the preview and subsequently in the work area, indicating that they have been applied.

The cut list on the left is also updated according to the newly applied working and the flute parameters.
Multiple workings of this type can be applied to a single cut, provided that their parameters are not duplicated.

DOC3.14 NESTING

The Nesting function automatically and optimally arranges pieces within the slab perimeter.

How to use the function

To use this function, create a piece list and define the perimeter in which the pieces are to be inserted.

Then press the button: the program automatically arranges the pieces within the slab perimeter.

NOTE

The pieces are placed on the slab taking into account subsequent use of the suction-cup material handling system to resolve collisions between pieces and the defects marked on the slab itself.

If the solution found is not satisfactory, press the button again to apply Nesting again and find a different configuration.

WARNING!

The program removes all pieces currently in the work area in order to perform Nesting.

The Nesting function arranges pieces according to different placement logics; therefore, each time the button is pressed, the program changes the piece arrangement, up to a maximum of 4 solutions (on the fifth attempt, the first solution is proposed again).
The program arranges the pieces in 4 different ways to allow the user to compare them and choose the best arrangement.

Some examples

Some examples of using the Nesting function are shown below.

  • It can be used to arrange simply shaped pieces more quickly.

  • This function finds the arrangement and combination of pieces that fills the largest possible slab area.

  • Nesting does not insert any piece inside the slab avoid areas.

  • Slab perimeters of any shape can be used.

  • If multiple perimeters are present, Nesting arranges pieces in each of them.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.14.1 AUTOMATIC NESTING (OPTIONAL)

Automatic Nesting is particularly useful when there are many pieces to process and the different combinations can no longer be easily managed manually.
Depending on the parameters set, different solutions may be available. They are shown on the screen and the operator can choose the preferred configuration.

Buttons

Add
The operator can create a configuration.

Delete
The operator can delete a configuration.

Edit
The operator can edit a configuration.

Execution
All configurations are calculated and the results are added to the list on the right.

Edit Configuration

Automatic Nesting allows customization of the parameters used to calculate piece placement within the work area for a configuration.
Depending on the type of pieces to be processed, some strategies may be better and more efficient.

Name

Name of the configuration as it appears in the list.

Distance Slab

Distance that pieces must maintain from the slab edge when they are positioned.

Num. solutions search

Number of solutions calculated by Nesting. The best one is selected from all calculated solutions.

Num. displacement tests

Number of attempts made by moving the piece if it does not fit within the slab perimeter.

Displacement value

Amount by which to move the piece when attempting to fit it within the slab perimeter.

Num. attempts on the same slab

Number of attempts allowed to insert the piece within the same perimeter if it does not fit.

Solutions calculation timeout

Maximum time allowed to calculate each individual solution.

Use list order

Forces the system to try to position the pieces within the perimeter following the order in which they appear in the piece list.

Use custom order

Allows the order in which pieces are tried for placement within the slab perimeter to be selected according to some of their properties.
To enable a sorting criterion, select the corresponding checkbox.
The criteria are applied from top to bottom. This means that the pieces are sorted according to the first criterion. If two or more pieces have the same value for the property associated with the first criterion, they are sorted according to the next criterion, and so on for each criterion in the list.
For each criterion, ascending or descending order can be selected.

Force piece before moving to next

Allows the system either to try placing the piece in different positions within the slab perimeter or to move on to the next piece without further attempts.

Fixed starting point

Allows selection of the perimeter point from which piece insertion starts.

Fix Rows - Columns Mode

Allows selection of whether pieces should be arranged by rows, by columns, or randomly during insertion.

Piece rotation mode

Allows selection of the logic used to rotate pieces during placement attempts within the slab perimeter.

Use largest inscribed rectangle

If enabled, the pieces are inserted within the largest-area rectangle contained within the perimeter.
Otherwise, Nesting attempts to arrange the pieces over the entire available perimeter surface.

Enable Deep Nesting

If disabled, the pieces are inserted on the slab so as to optimize use of the suction-cup material handling system for collision resolution.
If enabled, more complex piece combinations can be searched for, although their arrangement may collide with use of the handling system.

Running Nesting

Pressing the blue arrow next to each item in the list calculates Nesting using that configuration.
A preview of the result is added to the section on the right. It shows the arrangement of the pieces within the perimeter and the percentage of slab area covered by the pieces.

If the piece arrangement is not satisfactory, the blue arrow can be pressed again to recalculate the result.

After all Nesting configurations have been run, the results are arranged so that those occupying the largest slab area are shown first.

Once the preferred configuration has been selected, press the confirm button and the pieces are positioned on the slab according to the selected arrangement. The operator can still modify the position of the pieces in the work area.

NOTE

The pieces are placed on the slab taking into account subsequent use of the suction-cup material handling system to resolve collisions between pieces and the defects marked on the slab itself.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.15 INTERACTING WITH PIECES IN THE WORK AREA

The operator can change the positioning of pieces on the workbench by interacting with the work area.

Functions

Multiple selection
This function can be used to select or deselect multiple pieces at the same time.

Select all
This function can be used to select or deselect all pieces in the work area simultaneously.

Remove pieces
Removes the selected pieces from the work area.

Move pieces
Opens a panel that allows the selected pieces to be moved by specified distances.

Rotate pieces
Opens a panel that allows the selected pieces to be rotated by specified angles.

Undo operation
Undoes the last operation performed.

Magnetize pieces
Function that allows two cuts to be joined together.

Miter cut
Opens a panel that allows a cut on a piece in the work area to be inclined.

Edit commercial piece
Opens a panel that allows the dimensions of a commercial piece to be changed.

Select pieces

To select a piece, press inside it. The piece background is light blue when not selected and red when selected.

NOTE

Normally, only one piece can be selected at a time.

Multiple selection

Pressing the button enables multiple-selection mode. In this mode, multiple pieces can be selected at the same time. To deselect a piece, press inside a perimeter that is already selected.

Select all pieces

This button can be used to select or deselect all pieces in the work area simultaneously.

Remove pieces

Pressing the button removes the selected pieces from the work area and returns them to the piece list so that they are available later.

Move pieces

To move the selected piece, press and hold inside the perimeter and drag it in the work area.
Alternatively, use the movement panel with directional arrows.

NOTE

This function is applied to all selected pieces. Multiple pieces can therefore be moved simultaneously.

Buttons

Directional arrows
Buttons used to move the piece in different directions.
The movement distance can be set using the text box on the left.

Movement along the side axis
Allows movements parallel or orthogonal to the side of the selected piece.
If multiple pieces are selected simultaneously, they all move consistently relative to the selected side.

Move pieces along the standard axes

A movement of 1500 mm to the left is to be applied to the piece.

Move pieces along the side axis

A movement of 1500 mm to the left relative to the piece-side axis is to be applied to the piece.
To do this, the corresponding button must be enabled.

Rotate pieces

To rotate the selected pieces, press and hold outside the perimeter and drag them in the work area.
Alternatively, use the rotation panel with predefined angles.

NOTE

This function is applied to all selected pieces. Multiple pieces can therefore be rotated simultaneously.

Buttons

Clockwise rotation
Rotates the piece clockwise by the number of degrees specified in the text box below.

Counterclockwise rotation
Rotates the piece counterclockwise by the number of degrees specified in the text box below.

90_ rotation
Rotates the piece 90_ clockwise.

Apply rotation

A 45-degree clockwise rotation is to be applied to the piece.

Undo operation

This function undoes the last operation performed.
For example, if the operator deletes a piece by mistake, pressing this button returns to the state before the piece was deleted.

NOTE

There is no history of the changes made, but pressing the button multiple times undoes multiple operations.

How to load a state

In the same way, a previously programmed job can be loaded with all operations already performed.

This function is used to reload a previously saved job on the machine.

Import DXF (Optional)

This function loads the state of a job saved in a DXF file.

Import headings from DXF layout

It is now possible to import a slab into Parametrix with its heading cuts by drawing them on a dedicated layer of the DXF file.

The name of the layer dedicated to heading cuts must be defined together with a Donatoni technician. Once configured, it can no longer be changed.

Within this layer, each heading cut must be represented by a line.

WARNING!

When creating the DXF file, the following rules must be observed:
the slab perimeter must be present;
the slab perimeter must be rectangular;
the perimeter sides must be horizontal or vertical and must not be rotated;
each heading line must be parallel to one of the rectangle sides;
there must be at most one heading line for each side;
if multiple lines are drawn for the same side, Parametrix uses only the one closest to the edge.

To import the file, open the DXF Layout Import page in Parametrix and select the desired file.

Available settings

On the file selection screen, certain settings can be changed using the buttons below the preview on the right side of the screen.

Automatic mode
If the selected DXF file does not contain the heading-cuts layer, Parametrix adds them automatically based on the perimeter settings of http://pannello.Se if the layer is present, priority is given to the heading cuts
defined in the DXF file.

Magnet mode
Parametrix slightly moves the heading cuts to overlap the nearest cut, provided the distance between them is sufficiently small. This automatic correction can help optimize cut execution.

Magnet distance
Defines the maximum permitted distance between a heading cut and a piece cut for them to be overlapped using magnet mode. Heading-cut recognition is available both during standard import and during import with Slab Matching.

Examples

The images show a DXF file containing the slab perimeter, pieces and heading cuts, as well as the result obtained after import into Parametrix.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC3.17.1 SLAB MATCHING

This function allows the operator to load a cutting project prepared in the office and adapt it to the actual position and dimensions of the slab on the machine.

Buttons

X-Axis Offset
Displacement of the perimeter along the X axis relative to its original position.

Y-Axis Offset
Displacement of the perimeter along the Y axis relative to its original position.

Rotation
Difference in perimeter rotation relative to the starting condition.

Each button moves the perimeter in the direction indicated by the arrow.
The movement distance is specified in the text box below.

Clockwise/Counterclockwise Rotation
Allow the perimeter to be rotated counterclockwise and clockwise, respectively.
The rotation angle is specified in the text box below.

Reset Position

Automatic Slab Matching
Automatic perimeter alignment.

Show/Hide Pieces
Allows the perimeter of the pieces in the work area to be shown or hidden.

How to Use Slab Matching

The operator can plan a slab cutting project in the office using a photo taken from the easel and save it.

After taking a photo of the slab on the workbench, the machine operator can load the project file saved in the office using the Slab Matching function.

The window that opens shows the photo taken of the workbench and a preview of the perimeter of the slab programmed in the office.

The elements shown on the screen represent:

Blue

Perimeter of the slab programmed in the office.

Magenta

Perimeter of the pieces inside the slab programmed in the office.

Red

Original position of the slab programmed in the office.

Green

Position of the slab on the workbench.

The operator can move and/or rotate the perimeter within the work area to the correct position by dragging it, using the arrows, or using the automatic alignment button.
Once the perimeter has been positioned correctly, press confirm and the pieces will be shown positioned on the actual slab as in the file.

DOC3.21.1.1 EDIT CUT

This panel allows the operator to modify certain characteristics of a cut.

Buttons

In the top-left corner, the cut activation state can be modified.

Enable/Disable cut
Activates or deactivates the selected cut.

NOTE

A deactivated cut is not executed by the machine.

Different versions of this panel are displayed depending on the type of selected cut.

Disk Cuts

When a disk cut, either linear or arc, is selected, the following panel is displayed:

Disk cuts are characterized by a start point and an end point. The arrows define the direction of travel, from start to end.

The table below shows the buttons that allow the operator to modify the cut characteristics:

Reverse Cut Direction
The operator can reverse the cut execution direction.

Extension Amount
Allows the length of each cut extension to be modified.

Calculate Overcut
Recalculates the cut extension amount according to the disk diameter and material thickness so that it corresponds to the disk overcut.

Extend cut
Extends the cut by the length specified by the extension amount.
The left button extends the start of the cut, while the right button extends the end.

Shorten cut
Shortens the cut by the length specified by the extension amount.
The left button shortens the start of the cut, while the right button shortens the end.

Extend Start End to Slab Edge
Extends the start of the cut to the slab edge.
The value in the box is used when the cut is to be extended by a specified amount beyond the slab.

Extend Final End to Slab Edge
Extends the end of the cut to the slab edge.
The value in the box is used when the cut is to be extended by a specified amount beyond the slab.

Extend Short Cuts
If the selected cut is too short to allow the disk to penetrate the material completely, this button extends the cut, where possible, until it becomes a through cut.

Some data relating to cut execution are also displayed.

Plunge
Cut penetration into the material. The operator can modify this value.

Speed Percentage
Percentage of the set speed used to execute the cut. The operator can modify this value.

NOTE

The speed percentage of arc cuts cannot be modified.

Inclination
Cut inclination angle. Cannot be modified.

Edit the Cut from the Work Area

Selecting a cut in the work area and right-clicking opens a window for quickly modifying the cut.

The buttons correspond to the functions already listed. The end of the cut closest to the point where the button was pressed is extended.

Internal Arc Cuts

For arc cuts whose curvature faces toward the inside of the piece, it must be considered that disk overcut during machining could damage the side.
For this reason, these cuts must be executed differently from external cuts.

Parametrix provides two modes for cutting internal arcs, selectable with the button at the top right.

Inclined Arc
A miter cut is executed to size. The correct inclination is calculated automatically.

Offset Arc
The cut is executed without inclination but shifted toward the outside of the piece relative to its correct position.

NOTE

By default, Parametrix recommends setting these cuts to “inclined arc“ mode.
If this is not desired, the execution mode of each cut must be changed individually.

Each working mode has advantages and disadvantages:

  • Inclined arcs provide a better finish on the final result, which therefore requires less manual finishing work.
    However, they require greater effort from the machine, so the working must be performed at lower speeds and with more steps.

  • Offset arcs require less machine effort during working and can therefore be performed at higher speeds.
    On the other hand, disk overcut causes greater damage to the material, and more material must also be removed during manual finishing.

Holes and Milling Operations

Workings such as holes and milling operations allow fewer modifications by the operator.

Information is available for:

Plunge
Cut penetration into the material. The operator can modify this value.

Tool diameter
The diameter of the tool used for the cut is displayed.

Rims and Corner Holes

Corner holes and rims are workings composed of multiple holes and milling operations, respectively. When one of these items is selected, a list of all the cuts that make it up is displayed.

The operator can activate or deactivate each cut individually using the button on each list item, or act on all cuts in the working at the same time using the button at the top.
The buttons below the list allow the order in which the individual cuts are executed to be modified.

Move with arrows
Moves the selected cut to the position above or below.

Move to desired position
Moves the selected cut to the position specified in the adjacent text box.

In addition, the operator can modify the working penetration using the field below:

Plunge
Penetration of the cuts into the material. The operator can modify this value.

NOTE

The plunge depth of all cuts that make up the working is the same
Changing this value changes the penetration of all cuts in the list.

DOC3.21.4 MATERIAL HANDLING WITH SUCTION CUPS

This function allows the slab to be divided and the material to be moved using the suction cups.

Buttons

Manual Handling
Allows the operator to have full control over the movements to be performed.

Automatic Handling
Automatically performs the best movements.

Manual Handling

With this function, the operator can divide the slab using cuts and move the material to the desired position using the suction cups.
Depending on the number of selected cuts, this function has two modes.

Single-Selection Mode

To perform a movement using the suction cups, select a disk cut, either linear or arc, and press the button.
The cut is extended until it reaches the slab edge, when possible.
If the selected cut is inclined, a linear cut is automatically added specifically to allow the slab to be divided.

The following panel then opens, where the direction, orientation, and distance of the desired movement can be specified.

The following buttons are available in the section on the right:

Directional Movement
Moves one part of the cut slab in one of the directions.
The movement distance can be modified in the text box below.

Select an arrow in the work area or press one of the buttons on the right to choose the direction and orientation of the movement.
The slab is divided and moved according to the type of cut selected.
In both cases, the slab movement distance can be modified using the text box below the four directional buttons.

The selected cut is positioned as high as possible in the list of cuts to be performed. Immediately afterwards, the movement using the suction cups is executed.

WARNING!

The operator is responsible for verifying that the movement is feasible.

Multiple-Selection Mode

Multiple-selection mode allows pieces of any shape to be lifted. To do this, select the desired cuts for dividing the slab using multiple-selection mode.

Once the selection has been made, press the button to start the procedure.

The selected cuts are extended, where possible, to form a continuous path capable of dividing the slab. If one or more selected cuts are inclined, they are automatically replaced with non-inclined cuts.

The following panel then opens.

After selecting the slab section to move, the movement can be defined by dragging it in the work area or by using one of the following buttons:

Step
A value can be entered to specify the movement distance in mm when one of the directional buttons is pressed.

Movement Along the Axes
These boxes display values representing the slab displacement in the vertical and horizontal directions, respectively, relative to its starting position.
These values can be changed manually to define the slab movement.

Cut Collision Check
Parametrix automatically checks that, at the position to which the slab has been moved, no protruding cut will damage the other portion of material. If an anomaly is detected, the slab is moved to the nearest suitable position.
This check can be disabled to give the operator full control over the movement.

Restore Original Position
Allows the moved slab section to be reattached to its original position.

Upon confirmation, the selected cuts are positioned at the top of the list of cuts to be performed. Immediately afterwards, the movement using the suction cups is executed.

WARNING!

Multiple-selection mode allows pieces of any shape, including overhanging pieces, to be lifted.
The operator is responsible for verifying that the movement is feasible.

Rules for Valid Cut Selection

To divide the slab correctly, certain guidelines must be followed when selecting cuts.

  • The selected cuts may be disk cuts, both straight lines and arcs, milling operations, and multiple corner holes.

  • The selected cuts must be able to form a path that divides the slab in two. Selecting cuts that form a closed path is not allowed.

  • The program automatically extends linear disk cuts until it finds a solution that allows the slab to be divided. Arc cuts, milling operations, and holes are not modified automatically.
    Considering this, it is advisable for the first and last cuts in the path to be linear disk cuts.

  • If there are internal corners where disk overcut does not allow the material to be completely separated, corner milling operations or multiple holes must be inserted.

  • The penetration of the selected cuts must be sufficient to separate the slab.

  • The first and last cuts must be able to extend outside the slab.

Operation Not Possible Message

If the program determines that the handling operation is not possible, the causes may be the following:

  • The selected cuts are not sufficient to create a path that divides the slab in two;

  • The selected cuts form a closed path;

  • The selected cuts cannot detach the piece because of disk overcut;

  • Extending the selected cuts would damage other pieces;

  • The penetration of at least one of the selected cuts is not sufficient to separate the slab;

Automatic Handling

With this function, the program attempts to automatically resolve situations in which one or more pieces in the work area would be damaged by other cuts.

The algorithm analyzes the cut layout and independently determines how and where to perform the movements, optimizing the operation sequence.

However, automatic calculation cannot always handle every case. In particularly complex situations, manual intervention may be required to complete or correct the movements.

WARNING!

The operator is responsible for verifying that the movements are feasible.

Modify Suction Cup Position

During this phase, the operator can modify both the suction-cup gripping position and activation of the corresponding vacuum areas to ensure an optimal and safe grip on the material.
To do this, select the “Move“ item in the list and press the cut-edit button.

The buttons in this panel allow the operator to interact with the suction cups.

Directional Movement
They allow the suction-cup position to be modified.
The movement distance can be selected in the text box below.

NOTE

The suction cups can also be moved by interacting with them in the work area.

Suction Cup Rotation
Rotates the suction cups around their axis.
The value in the text box alongside indicates how far the suction-cup unit rotates each time the arrows are clicked.

Suction Cup Unit Diagram
The suction-cup unit diagram allows the operator to select which vacuum areas are switched on or off during movement. If an area is green, the machine activates the vacuum; if it is red, it does not.
On the left is an example with areas 5 and 6 switched off.

Contains operations that allow the working order to be modified.

List of operations that move cuts belonging to a working type to the top of the list.

Move Workings to Bottom

This option can be enabled to reverse the operation order.

Because the positions are overwritten, this option is available to make the operation order chronological.

Activating a Macro

Once the macro has been created and modified as desired, it can be selected and activated.

Enable Macro Disabled
Each deselected macro has, immediately to its right, the button for activating the macro in the disabled state.

Enable Macro Enabled
The currently selected macro, which has not yet been activated, has the same button as the others, but it is green to indicate that activation can proceed.

Macro Activated
The currently loaded macro is highlighted in green and has a symbol immediately to its right confirming that it has been loaded.
The name of the loaded macro is also visible in the parameter User Values, under “Active Operation”:

Macro Creation and Loading Procedure

The first step is to make sure that the activation button is set to ON, so that the desired macro can subsequently be used.

Proceed by creating a new operation and assigning it a name. Then click the new operation now visible in the list and immediately afterwards the edit button on the right side of the panel to access the panel used to modify the macro.
For each operation type, select the desired operations from the list on the left (Available) and add them to the list of selected operations. The configuration can then be confirmed so that it can be viewed and managed in the operations panel.
The macro can be loaded by clicking the button immediately to the right of the macro name.
The following example shows the macro named “operation_1“, containing 3 operations visible on the right and highlighted in green with the corresponding symbol because it is in the “loaded“ state.

The first step is to make sure that the activation button is set to ON, which is required in order to use the desired macro. Once enabled, create a new operation and assign it an identifying name. After creation, the operation appears in the list: select it and click the edit button on the right side of the panel to access the macro configuration interface.

Within this interface, for each operation type, the desired items can be selected from the list on the left (labeled "Available") and added to the list on the right, which represents the selected operations. Once the selection is complete, confirm the configuration to make it visible and manageable in the operations panel.

The macro can be loaded by clicking the dedicated button immediately to the right of the assigned macro name. As an example, consider the macro named “operation_1”: it includes three operations displayed in the panel on the right and is highlighted in green with the corresponding symbol indicating its “loaded” state.

DOC3.21.8 ISO CONTROL PAGE

This screen allows real-time monitoring of the ISO program being executed by the machine.

Preview

The center section of the screen shows the machine movement in real time in the work area.
Piece cuts that have already been executed are colored green, while those still to be executed retain their original color.

Working Name and Elapsed Time
The name of the program being executed and the time the machine is taking to execute it are displayed.

Motor

This section displays information about the machine motors.

Motor

Main spindle motor.

External Motor

Tool Plus motor, if present.

The information tab can be changed using the buttons below.

Previous/Next Information Panel
These buttons allow the operator to change the category of information displayed.

For each motor, the following is shown:

Intake

Indicates the current drawn by the motor.

Ampere threshold

Indicates the Ampere threshold above which the alarm is activated and motor rotation is stopped.
It is recommended to set the value according to the mounted tool and the working being performed.

RPM

Indicates the number of motor revolutions per minute.
If the rotation direction is clockwise, the value is positive. If the direction is counterclockwise, the sign is negative.

Axes

This section displays information about the machine axes.

Real

The instantaneous coordinates relating to the position and orientation of the machine axes are displayed.

Distance To Go

Displays the distance of each axis from the coordinates at which the cut ends.

Intake

Displays the electrical current consumption of each axis motor.

Tool

This section displays data relating to the tool currently being used for the cut.

Name

The type and name of the tool used during the working are displayed.

Feed

Machine movement speed along the direction of travel.

Thickness

Penetration of the cut currently being executed on the slab.

Manual controls

If problems occur during execution of the working, some machine functions can be controlled using manual commands.

Manual controls
Opens the manual-command window for controlling water and suction cups.

Water

Internal water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply through the inside of the tool.
The indicator above the button changes color: Green = On; Red = Off.

Water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply from the main line.
The indicator above the button changes color: Green = On; Red = Off.

Suction cups

Enable / disable suction cups
The screen shows the suction cup assembly viewed from above, divided into its various zones. Pressing the relevant area changes its status.
Green indicates that the zone is set for vacuum.
Red indicates that the zone is set for blowing.

SUCTION CUPS: RAISE - Suction cup parking
When the button is pressed, the suction cups are retracted to the rest/parking position.

SUCTION CUPS: LOWER - Prepare suction cups
When the button is pressed, the suction cups are lowered from the parking position to the limit stop. It is important that there is enough space for the suction cups to extend completely.

LIFT PIECE: RELEASE - Unload piece
When the button is pressed, the Z axis is lowered until the material contacts the work surface, the vacuum pump is switched off, and blowing is activated from all suction cups to release the piece. After a timeout, the axis is raised to the safety position.

LIFT PIECE: START - Lift piece
With this command, the suction cups are brought into contact with the material, the vacuum pump is switched on in the areas marked green and blowing is activated in the areas marked red; once the vacuum switch indicates that vacuum has been generated, the axis is raised to the position set for movements.

WARNING!

Pay attention to the active suction cups and use the largest possible area to lift the piece.

BLOW - Blow control
The button switches blowing on or off from suction cups that are not set for vacuum. The indicator shows whether blowing is on (green) or off (red).

VACUUM - Vacuum pump control
This button switches the vacuum pump on and off. The indicator shows whether the pump is on (green) or off (red).

DOC3.22.1 EASY MATCH (OPTIONAL)

With the Easy Match function, the operator can see in real time the background that pieces will have in the original position in which they were designed while moving them on the workbench over a slab.

Buttons

Preview View

Allows pieces to be moved by clicking inside the perimeter of the piece itself, making it possible to position the piece in the desired location more precisely.

The preview displays all pieces from the imported file in the exact position in which they were designed.
The preview size corresponds at a 1:1 scale to the dimensions of the designed pieces.
Pieces added to the workbench take on the slab color, while pieces still to be added have a uniform background.

From the preview it is possible to:

  • Add a piece to the work area by clicking inside the area to be processed.

  • Move a piece located on the workbench.

  • Select a piece on the workbench by clicking inside the piece.

  • Delete a piece from the preview by selecting the eraser below the piece list and then selecting the piece in the preview to be deleted. In this case, the piece is also deleted from the workbench and from the piece list.

Side-by-Side View

Displays both the project preview and the workbench on the same screen.

Allows the preview of the current working to be saved.
The following screen opens:

The operator is asked to choose the preview name, whether to save it as an image or PDF, where to save it, and its resolution.
For the resolution, the available choices are auto (automatic resolution), low, medium, high, ultra, and custom (the operator chooses the exact resolution).
Once confirmed, the preview photo or PDF opens automatically.

Edit preview

On this screen, the pieces that make up the preview can be arranged as desired.
All changes made here are also reflected later in the other views.

The following buttons are available on the top bar.

Move pieces
Allows the pieces that make up the preview to be moved.
Displays the buttons on the bottom bar of the window.

Pan view
Used to move the preview view containing all pieces.

Preview Customization

In the program parameters panel, on the user values tab, the colors of some elements in the project preview can be changed.

Perimeter

Shows/hides the perimeter of the pieces in the preview.
The display color can be changed using the adjacent button.

Name

Shows/hides the names of the pieces in the preview.
The display color can be changed using the adjacent button.

Background

Sets the preview background color.

Remove Background
Removes the background from the preview.

Workflow

To work using Easy Match, the project must be imported into Parametrix from a DXF file.
The program displays a Book Match preview for the pieces contained in the file.

After taking a photo of the workbench, the pieces to be cut can be placed on the slab.
To do this, use the standard procedure from the piece list or press inside the perimeter of one of the pieces shown in the preview.

Dragging the piece from the preview also moves it on the slab, which is useful for matching the veining between the various pieces.
The reverse can also be done: drag the piece from the slab and use the preview to check whether the veining matches depending on where it is moved.

At this point, proceed with the standard working procedure: create the ISO program and cut the slab.
Once finished, press the button to move to the next working.
The preview retains the project progress status.
Proceed by acquiring a photo of a new slab and placing the pieces inside the perimeter.

Continue in this way until the project is completed.

When Nesting is activated for the entire project, two modes become available.

Slabs are created and Nesting is applied until all pieces in the list have been used.
The slab dimensions are the same as those of the first slab that was defined.
This is used to provide an indication of how many slabs may be required to complete the project when slabs of the same shape are to be cut.

To use Nesting until all pieces are used, a perimeter must be created to provide the program with the dimensions of the slabs that will be used.

DOC3.23 UNLOAD PIECE (OPTIONAL)

This function can be used to program movement of a piece to a predefined machine position.
The program calculates movement of the piece center to an X, Y and Z machine coordinate defined in the parameters. 

Methods for adding Unload Piece

Single
Applies a single operation to a selected piece.

All pieces
Applies piece unloading to every piece inserted in the work area.

Single

After enabling single mode, click the piece to be unloaded.
The following example image shows the function applied to the piece in the center, with the corresponding addition of a cut to the cut list on the right:

All pieces

This mode automatically unloads all pieces in the work area. The corresponding cuts are consequently added to the list displayed in the right-hand side panel.
An example after executing the mode is shown below:

Required precautions

The program does not perform checks to prevent material movement in certain special situations that may occur.
These checks are the responsibility of the machine operator.

Particular attention must be paid to the following situations:

  • Miter cuts: if the piece has miter cuts, the piece may remain trapped in the slab.

  • Piece with cuts flush with the disk: the piece may not be completely cut; in this case, when the function attempts to lift the piece, it will remain attached to the slab.

  • Cuts inside the perimeter: if there are cuts inside the piece perimeter, check and, if necessary, move the suction cup positions to allow vacuum to be generated.

DOC3.26 CUT SIMULATION

This function allows a simulation of the operations performed on the piece to be viewed.

 

 

Buttons

The button for accessing the cut simulation function is located on the bottom bar of the Parametrix cut-editing screen.

Cut simulation
This button opens and closes the cut simulation screen.

 

Cut simulation management

The simulation is controlled by these buttons:

Start
This button starts the simulation.

Pause
This button temporarily pauses the simulation.

Restart
This button restarts the simulation from the beginning.

Simulation speed
This button adjusts the simulation execution speed by selecting one of three available levels.

 

Cut simulation

The simulation starts with the machine in the parking position. The milling cutter or disk then performs the cuts according to the sequence defined in the queue shown in the right-hand column. At the end of each step, the completed item is highlighted in green.

Different actions or events can be added to the simulation queue and their order changed, allowing the sequence to be adapted to the specific machining requirements and making the simulation more effective for its intended purpose.

DOC4 PARAMETRIX SX

Parametrix includes a version specifically designed to facilitate the workflow on machines belonging to the SX category.
In particular, it allows the operator to efficiently manage cut combinations in order to optimize the production process.
This chapter describes functions that differ from the standard Parametrix version.

Side section

The buttons located at the top right allow the operator to change the Parametrix screen.

Each screen handles a specific aspect of slab machining.

Piece positioning
Parametrix main screen.
Operations performed include:

  • creating and editing pieces;

  • acquiring the slab photo on the workbench and its perimeter;

  • positioning pieces in the work area;

Cut optimization and management
Screen for optimizing and managing cuts.
Operations managed include:

  • moving the material with suction cups;

  • washing the workbench;

  • editing cuts to optimize their combinations;

Cut combination
Final screen of the workflow.
Operations managed include:

  • displaying and sorting cut combinations;

  • unloader management;

  • starting the machine cutting program;

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC4.1 MANUAL CONTROLS PAGE

When the application starts, if the axes have already been zeroed, the following initial screen is displayed:

WARNING!

When starting the machine, maximum care must be taken when moving axes before the zeroing procedure has been performed; collisions with the machine mechanical limit stops may occur and compromise correct machine operation.

Top bar

Parameters
Provides access to the Parametrix program parameters.

Parameters tool
Pressing the button opens the tool parameters page. See the “Tool Configuration” chapter for a detailed description of the parameters page.

Automatic 0/90-degree rotation
The “C” axis is automatically moved to either 0 or 90 degrees when the button is pressed.

Automatic parking
When pressed, the machine automatically moves the “X”, “Y”, “Z” and “C” axes to their zero positions.
The machine performs the movements in the following order:
(A) - “Z” axis to the absolute zero position;
(B) - “C” axis to the absolute 0 position;
(C) - “X” and “Y” axes simultaneously to the absolute zero position;

WARNING!

Certain safety conditions must be met in order to perform automatic parking:
The “A” axis position must be 0_.
Make sure that the movement area involved in positioning (see figure alongside) is clear.

Zero
Performs axis zeroing (this operation is required when the machine is started or when the rectangular indicators are red).
When the zeroing cycle is complete, the indicators turn gray.
The zeroing procedure includes sequential movement of the axes:

  1. Z axis

  2. A axis

  3. C axis

  4. X and Y axes simultaneously

  5. B axis (Optional: controlled lathe)

NOTE

Zeroing is permitted only when the coded key is inserted in the designated position on the operator console.

Internal water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply through the inside of the tool.
The indicator above the button changes color: Green = On; Red = Off.

Water ON/OFF
Pressing this button activates the water supply from the main line.
The indicator above the button changes color: Green = On; Red = Off.

Manual Tool Change
Pressing the button starts the tool change procedure.

Maintenance
Pressing this button displays a window containing all machine maintenance operations.
Both maintenance operations that need to be performed and those within normal limits are displayed.
If at least one maintenance operation requires it.

Help
Pressing this button slightly changes the appearance and behavior of all buttons currently visible. You can then press any button with a small question mark in the upper-left corner to learn about the function provided by that button through a short message. To exit this help mode, simply press the “Help” button again.

Right sidebar

When the application starts, the preselected function is MANUAL.
This sidebar contains the following available commands and programs/functions:

Central area

The central area consists of the following elements, described in detail below:

  • Axes

  • Controls

  • Disk management

  • Suction cups

Axes

This interface displays the machine axis values.

Example of the “Axes” interface element with origin 0 and the axes already zeroed:

Example of the “Axes” interface element with origin 0 and the axes not yet zeroed:

The elements making up this section of the common interface are explained below, using the elements shown when the axes have already been zeroed as reference.

Actual position: indicates the axis position relative to the active origin.
Target position: indicates the position to be set in order to move the axis by pressing the MDI or RTCP button.
F: Feed, movement speed expressed in mm/minute.
DTG: Distance To Go, distance from the target.
A: Ampere.

Axis Reset
Pressing this button sets the zero point of the active origin at the current position of the corresponding axis (X, Y or Z).
The axis reset operation can only be performed on origins other than 0 (zero).
To use the tool-coordinate origin (TCP), the correct dimensions of the mounted tool must be set before pressing the Axis Reset button.

Automatic _90-degree rotation
The “C” axis position is increased by 90 degrees clockwise.
Example: if the machine is at 12 degrees, pressing the “Automatic _90-degree rotation” button moves the machine to 102 degrees: 12 _ 90.

Automatic -90-degree rotation
The “C” axis position is decreased by 90 degrees counterclockwise.
Example: if the machine is at 102 degrees, pressing the “Automatic -90-degree rotation” button moves the machine to 12 degrees: 102 - 90.

Controls

This panel contains several buttons whose behavior is explained below:

MAN (Enable manual movement)
To use the machine in manual mode, the spindles must be positioned correctly and certain functions must be enabled. This button is provided for this purpose.

NOTE

When manual operation is enabled, the adjacent indicator LED turns green.

Suction cup axis
Reference axis on which the suction cups are mounted.

Ampere threshold
Indicates the threshold above which the alarm is activated and spindle rotation is stopped.

Selected origin
Clicking the “Origin” field allows the operator to change the origin to be used.
Changing this field triggers an update of the Axes values.
Origin values can range from 0 to 19 inclusive.

MDI
When pressed, the machine moves until the positions set as target positions are reached (see above).
The speed of the X and Y axes is controlled by their respective potentiometers, while the other axes are controlled by the interpolated potentiometer.

Disk management

Only one of the windows available to the operator for managing the installed disks is shown below, as the remaining windows have similar functions.

First reference axis
First reference axis for each disk (X1 for DISK1 in the example)

NOTE

When positioning the X axes, the center of the disk is used as the reference for the target
position; the current position differs by half the disk core thickness.

Second reference axis
Second reference axis for each disk (Z1 for DISK1 in the example)

Start/Stop spindle rotation
Controls starting and stopping of the disk on the corresponding spindle.
The disk speed is selected in the tool parameters.

Enable/Disable spindle external water
Allows starting and stopping of the water supply for the selected tool to be controlled.

Intake
Indicates the current drawn by the spindle motor.

Feed

The Feed value represents the interpolated movement of the machine.

Suction cups

The suction cups can be used manually to move pieces from one work zone to another.

Suction cup buttons

Enable / disable suction cups
The screen shows the suction cup assembly viewed from above, divided into its various zones. Pressing the relevant area changes its status.
Green indicates that the zone is set for vacuum.
Red indicates that the zone is set for blowing.

SUCTION CUPS: RAISE - Suction cup parking
When the button is pressed, the suction cups are retracted to the rest/parking position.

SUCTION CUPS: LOWER - Prepare suction cups
When the button is pressed, the suction cups are lowered from the parking position to the limit stop. It is important that there is enough space for the suction cups to extend completely.

LIFT PIECE: RELEASE - Unload piece
When the button is pressed, the Z axis is lowered until the material contacts the work surface, the vacuum pump is switched off, and blowing is activated from all suction cups to release the piece. After a timeout, the axis is raised to the safety position.

LIFT PIECE: START - Lift piece
With this command, the suction cups are brought into contact with the material, the vacuum pump is switched on in the areas marked green and blowing is activated in the areas marked red; once the vacuum switch indicates that vacuum has been generated, the axis is raised to the position set for movements.

WARNING!

Pay attention to the active suction cups and use the largest possible area to lift the piece.

VACUUM - Vacuum pump control
This button switches the vacuum pump on and off. The indicator shows whether the pump is on (green) or off (red).

BLOW - Blow control
The button switches blowing on or off from suction cups that are not set for vacuum. The indicator shows whether blowing is on (green) or off (red).

Safety conditions

Pay particular attention to the active suction cups during lifting, ensuring that the areas used are sufficient to lift the piece being moved. Always try to use the largest available vacuum area to grip the piece and check that there are no defects or breaks in the material that could create hazards or machine operating problems.
Once the vacuum pump has been switched on, it may only be switched off using the automatic functions provided for this purpose. Pressing the reset button or the emergency stop mushroom has no effect on the vacuum pump, which will continue to operate. The pump can be forcibly switched off using the dedicated button on the “Additional Controls” page.
During automatic procedures, before lifting the piece, the vacuum status is checked by a dedicated sensor: if a sufficient vacuum value is not detected, the “vacuum missing” alarm appears. The pump will remain active until the vacuum switch detects a correct value or until it is disabled from the “Additional Controls” page.

WARNING!

Loss of power to the vacuum pump causes a rapid loss of vacuum and consequently causes the material lifted by the suction cups to fall.

Bottom bar

The bottom bar displays information and error messages as well as buttons for certain functions.
Three examples of the bottom bar are shown below:

  • With no active alarms.

  • With a general emergency active, shown with an icon, an error code (PE0000 in this example), the related description, and the alarm button on the right flashing.

  • With a displayed message, direct JOG active in the example.

Alarms
Allows the operator to access the alarm window.

Minimize software
Allows the operator to exit the software page.

Machine shutdown
Allows the operator to completely shut down the machine.

Alarms

The alarms page shows the active system Alarms/Messages.
If the machine has no active alarms, the page is empty; otherwise, one row is displayed for each current error.
The following example page for alarm management and display shows an alarm currently active in the system:

Alarm buttons

Updates
Used to refresh the status of the machine alarms.

Alarm history
Allows the daily alarm history to be displayed.

Messages / Alarms
Allows you to choose whether to display alarms or messages.

Alarm groups
Shows complete information about the alarms currently present on the machine.

Alarm display - Standard

The standard display of one of the alarms consists of:

Online link
A button with a link to the relevant online guide.

Alarm code
Identification code of the problem that caused the alarm.

Description
A brief description of the detected error.

Alarm display - History

In addition to the items already described, the daily alarm history also includes the following data:

Status change time
Date and time when the alarm status changed.

Alarm status
Status reached by the alarm (ON / OFF).

Alarm display - Groups

The grouping system displays a single entry for each alarm, avoiding duplicates.

Number of occurrences
The number of times the alarm has been activated.

First activation time
Date and time of the first alarm activation.

Last activation time
Date and time of the most recent alarm activation.

DOC4.1.1 ISO PROGRAM LIST

The ISO File Program List page allows multiple programs previously created using CAD-CAM software to be executed consecutively, for machines with two work areas, Twin machines, or programs with multiple machining operations created while the machine is already running.

Top bar

The top bar displays information for monitoring the progress status of the list.

List execution status
Indicates whether the list is currently running.

List progress bar
Shows the progress and execution status of the list.

List progress bar

This progress bar provides information on the execution status of the current ISO program while also giving an overview of the next program in the list and the program that has already completed machining and moved to unloading.

In the previous image, no program is yet shown as unloading because execution of the list has not started and no pieces have been processed. Conversely, if there is only one ISO file in the list or the job has been started and all other files have already been executed, the ‘Next’ section will be empty.

During execution, program progress is displayed in real time, as shown below.

Side menu

On the right side of the suction cup panel there are several buttons for managing the individual files in the program list.

Execute next program
This button moves the current program to unloading and loads the next program.

Move selected item up
Moves the selected ISO file upward within the list of files to be executed.

Move selected item down
Moves the selected ISO file downward within the list of files to be executed.

Delete selected item
Removes the currently selected item from the list.
If multiple items are selected, only the first selected item is deleted.

Suction cup panel
Opens the panel for managing suction cup zones.

Conveyor panel
Provides access to the conveyor management panel.

Conveyor Panel

The page is used to manage slab loading and unloading through the conveyor belt located under the machine.

WARNING!

Before operating the conveyor controls, check the work area both at the line inlet and outlet to ensure that no people are present and to avoid unnecessary risks.

Top-bar buttons

Automatic slab loading
Starts the loading cycle, which follows this sequence:

  1. Moves the loading roller conveyor until the slab contacts belt #1

  2. Moves the belts until the incoming slab reaches the preset position. The slab position is referenced to the inlet edge.

Unload pieces
Starts belt movement to carry the material out of the work area. The travel distance is set in the software parameters.

Conveyor parameters

The page contains flags used to select machine-specific options.

Move the tape at the program end

Enables automatic movement of machined pieces to the unloading area at the end of the executed program.

Enable robot

Enables the robot.

Wait for picture

Stops execution of the program list after each execution

Internal washing

Enables internal washing.

Lower washing

Enables washing of the upper surface of the slab.

Upper washing

Enables slab washing.

Bottom-bar buttons

Using the dedicated buttons, the conveyor can be moved either to the right or to the left.

Manual conveyor movement to the left
The conveyor moves to the left.

Manual conveyor movement to the right
The conveyor moves to the right.

Bottom bar

The lower part of the bar displays several functions relating to execution of the ISO program list, as well as monitoring of both the tool and the slab.

List execution management

At the bottom there are also two buttons relating to program execution modes:

Manual / automatic
Defines whether the machine status is manual or automatic.

Single / next automatic
Defines whether the next program will start automatically or not.

Slab and probing-cycle monitoring

At the center and right of the bottom bar, the operator can configure periodic tool diameter monitoring by setting checks at defined intervals based on the number of cycles performed.

Number of Cycles Between Disks' Probes
Sets the number of programs to execute before performing a probe to measure the disk diameters.

Number of Cycles To The Next Probe
Indicates the number of cycles remaining before the next disk probing operation.

Slab thickness
Displays the slab thickness.

ISO Program List Execution

The ISO program list is automatically expanded as ISO files are generated in Parametrix; however, the operator can reposition items within the list or remove them according to requirements.

Before executing the list, the operator can set the number of cycles to be performed between tool probing operations.
The number of cycles remaining until the next probing operation is then updated and displayed.

The operator starts execution of the program list by pressing the “Cycle Start” button. The programs are then executed sequentially, simultaneously displaying the current program, the program to be executed next, and the program already completed.

If the program execution mode is set to Manual and Single, list execution is interrupted at the end of the current program, immediately after preparing the next program to be executed.
In this case, the operator can press the Next button at the most appropriate time and proceed with execution by pressing the 'Cycle Start' button again.

DOC4.2 TOOL PANEL

This panel allows the operator to manage the machine disks.

Parameters

The parameters of the selected disk set are shown in this section.
The general parameters of the disk set are shown on the left, while the parameters specific to the disk associated with each positioner are shown on the right.
For SX5 or SX6 machines, 5 and 6 disks respectively are shown in the right-hand section.

General disk-set parameters

The parameters in the left-hand section relating to the selected disk set are listed below.

Name
Name of the disk set.

Radius
Radius of the disks in the set.

NOTE

All disks in the set must have the same diameter.

Disk thickness
Average thickness of the disks in the set.

RPM
Revolutions per minute of the motors on which the disks are mounted.

Junction Quote
Clearance position of the disk set.

The following buttons are also available:

Recalculate thickness
Recalculates the average thickness of the disks.

RPM information
Opens a table containing recommended RPM values for machine operation.

Individual disk parameters

Each of these elements shows the parameters of the disk mounted on the corresponding positioner.

For each disk, radius and thickness can be set. The operator can decide whether to enable the disk using the adjacent button.

Enable/Disable disk
Indicates whether or not to use the disk mounted on the corresponding positioner.

Buttons

Probe disk
Starts a disk probing cycle.

Compensation
Provides access to the window for manual compensations.

Complete data
Provides access to the window for editing disk data.

Complete data

In this window, the operator can edit all data relating to the disk set mounted on the machine.
In particular, the radius, tooth thickness and core thickness of each disk can be set.

In particular:

Disk thickness
Measurement of the disk tooth thickness.

Core thickness
Measurement of the disk core thickness.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC4.2.1 COMPENSATIONS

This function allows manual compensations to be applied to the distance between the machine positioners.
It should be used if a discrepancy is observed between the dimensions of the programmed pieces and the measurements observed on the resulting pieces.

Required values

During the compensation procedure, the operator is asked to enter these values.

Desired piece dimensions

Programmed dimension of the side of the pieces to be checked.

Piece

Measured dimension of the side of the piece whose ends were cut using the indicated disk and the next disk.

Thickness

Thickness of the disk mounted on the indicated positioner.

Finally, press the button.

Compensation
Apply the appropriate compensation.

Procedure to follow

First, import two rectangular pieces with the same dimensions into Parametrix.
They must be arranged side by side on a slab as shown in the figure, then proceed with machining.

Open the manual positioner-compensation window and complete the required fields.
The original dimension of the programmed rectangle side must be entered.
Then enter the measured dimensions of the same side of each cut rectangle, taking care to indicate which disks were used.
Finally, enter the thickness of each disk mounted on the machine.

At the end, press the button below to have Parametrix calculate the compensation to apply to each positioner.

NOTE

Depending on the number of machine positioners, more rectangles of suitable dimensions for the workbench must be cut.
