DOC4.3 CUT OPTIMIZATION AND MANAGEMENT

The second button at the top right opens the cut optimization and management screen.

Cut list

The cuts to be performed by the machine are listed here.

Using the cut list, the operator can:

  • Change the cut execution order.

  • Edit the characteristics of a cut.

  • Insert pauses between cuts.

List elements

Enable/Disable cut
Indicates whether the cut is enabled or disabled for the job.
Pressing the button changes its status.

Cut type
Indicates the cut type (“Perimeter”, “Internal Cut”, “Milling”, etc.).

Functions

The arrangement of the cuts in the list on the right indicates the order in which they are performed.
Using the buttons below, this order can be changed or a pause can be inserted in the execution of operations between one cut and the next.

Edit cut
Allows certain properties of the selected cut to be edited.

Insert pause
A pause can be inserted between execution of the selected cut and the next cut.
The program performs all cuts preceding the pause, then stops the machine and waits for the operator to issue the Start command.
It can be used, for example, to change the tool.

Delete cut
When this function is enabled, an eraser-shaped icon is displayed next to each entry in the cut list.
Pressing this icon allows the user to permanently remove the corresponding cut from the list.

Cut optimization
Used to improve the combination of machine spindles during cutting.
The mode must be specified in the adjacent text box and the button pressed to apply the optimizations.

Additional piece properties
Allows the additional properties of the selected piece in the work area to be edited.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC4.3.1 CUT OPTIMIZATION

On the cut-management page, optimizations can be applied for the SX machine to improve spindle combinations during cutting.

Mode 1

This mode joins two different cuts located on the same straight line, turning them into a single cut.

Mode 2

Attempts to make all cuts the same (maximum) length.

Mode 3

Normally, after using the movement system it is impossible to manually move execution of a cut before the movement.
With this optimization mode, the software places before the movement the cuts that the machine can perform.

Mode 4

Cuts of similar length become cuts of the same length.

Mode 5

Extends all cuts beyond the slab edge and makes them similar in length, as in mode 2.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC4.4 CUT COMBINATION

This screen shows the spindle combinations used by the machine to perform cuts.

Combined cut list

Each item in the list in the right-hand section shows the combination of spindles used to perform a set of cuts simultaneously.

NOTE

If a spindle is manually disabled using the dedicated command in the tool panel, it is not considered in the cut combinations.

As with standard cuts, their order in the list can be changed or they can be disabled.

Enable/Disable cut
Indicates whether the cut is enabled or disabled for the job.
Pressing the button changes its status.

Move with arrows
Moves the selected cut to the position above or below.

Move to desired position
Moves the currently selected cut to the position specified in the adjacent text box.

Pause
Allows a pause to be inserted immediately after the selected cut.

NOTE

Any operation performed on a list item affects all the cuts it contains.

Buttons

The following button is located on the bottom bar:

Display Unloading
Provides access to a screen through which the operator can create an unloading program to position rows of pieces on the dedicated conveyor belts.

Machine technical documentation Operational document

DOC4.4.1 UNLOADER

The strip unloader is managed by the software by creating an unloading program to position rows of pieces on the dedicated belts and to verify gripping positions and the zones used.

Executing the machining operation

The software checks that the slab is divided into horizontal rows (with a tolerance of a few degrees in cut direction), that piece dimensions are within the limits, and sets the movement order and the row of suction cups to use.
Movements with the suction cups to the right or left, intersecting pieces, and other similar conditions prevent creation of the program, which will not be unloaded automatically.

Gripping zones are shown in green, while non-gripping zones are shown in red.
The parameters are set by the technician when the machine is commissioned and remain fixed.
